articles.standfirst: Series Even at 1-1: A'ja Wilson's Aces and Caitlin Clark's Fever trade blows in Vegas
articles.summary: Series Even at 1-1: A'ja Wilson's Aces and Caitlin Clark's Fever trade blows in Vegas
articles.body:
The WNBA Playoff series between the Las Vegas Aces and Indiana Fever has become exactly the heavyweight scrap the seeding promised, and now it comes down to nerve. After splitting the first two games, the two sides return to Michelob Ultra Arena in Las Vegas locked at one win apiece, a knife's-edge situation in which every possession carries the weight of a season.

What time is and Where to watch the Las Vegas Aces vs Indiana Fever game 3 tonight?

Tip-off for the Las Vegas Aces vs Indiana Fever game 3 is set for this Thursday, October 1, 2026, at 9:00 p.m. ET (8:00 p.m. Central Time and 6:00 p.m. Pacific Time) . The venue is Michelob Ultra Arena in Las Vegas, a 12,000-seat building that has been a fortress for the Aces all year.

As for where you’ll be able to watch it, the WNBA Playoff basketball is carried across the league's national rights partners, but for the Las Vegas Aces vs Indiana Fever game 3 you can catch it:

TV Channel: USA Network and CNBC

The Split: How the series got here

Las Vegas struck first, taking Game 1 on their home floor by a commanding 102-85. That opener was a masterclass in efficiency: the Aces shot 59% from the field (38-of-64), buried nine three-pointers, and never trailed by more than two points, controlling the lead for over 35 of the game's 40 minutes and stretching their advantage to as many as 27. They out-rebounded Indiana 31-24 and blocked six shots to Indiana's zero.

Indiana answered in Game 2, flipping the script with a 99-89 road-turned-home win to level the series. The bounce-back was authored by Caitlin Clark , who stuffed the stat sheet with 27 points, 15 assists, and seven rebounds while knocking down five three-pointers — a nine-plus rating performance that tilted the floor.

Kelsey Mitchell added 26 points on a perfect blend of drives and free throws (9-of-11 from the line), and Aliyah Boston bullied the paint for 22 points on 10-of-15 shooting with five assists. When the Fever get all three of that trio going, they are as dangerous as anyone left standing.

Las Vegas Aces vs Indiana Fever: Regular-Season standings

Both teams arrive as legitimate contenders. In the Western Conference, Las Vegas finished third at 31-13, trailing only the Minnesota Lynx (33-11) and Golden State Valkyries (32-12). Indiana closed the Eastern Conference in third at 28-16, level on wins with the Washington Mystics but behind the top-seeded Atlanta Dream (30-14). In the combined league table, the Aces ranked third overall and the Fever sixth — a small gap that has looked even smaller once the ball has gone up in this series.

What swings at Las Vegas Aces vs Indiana Fever Game 3?

The numbers point to a few clear battlegrounds. Rebounding was decisive in Game 1, where the Aces controlled the defensive glass 26-16; if Boston and the Fever front line can flip that edge, Indiana earns extra possessions Clark can weaponize.

Shooting variance matters too — Las Vegas can win the math when they're at 59% from the floor, but Indiana's shot-making (12 threes in Game 2) gives them the ceiling to trade haymakers. Free throws loom large as well: both Wilson and Young were automatic at the stripe in Game 2, and in a series this tight, whoever draws contact and converts down the stretch may decide it.

Prediction for the Las Vegas Aces vs Indiana Fever Game 3

Home court has meant a great deal in this matchup — the Aces were dominant in Game 1 at Michelob Ultra Arena, controlling the game wire to wire, and they get the building back for Game 3. But Indiana has already shown it can win when Clark, Mitchell, and Boston all click.

Expect a tight, high-possession contest that comes down to the final minutes. The edge, narrowly, goes to Las Vegas at home behind Wilson and Young — but don't be surprised if this one is decided by a single possession, with the Aces edging ahead to reclaim the series lead.

articles.title: ‘Classless’: WNBA fans slam Angel Reese after controversial post-game gesture to Mystics
articles.standfirst: Reese’s gesture sparks backlash as Atlanta advances to the WNBA semifinals
articles.summary: Reese’s gesture sparks backlash as Atlanta advances to the WNBA semifinals
articles.body:
Angel Reese is facing criticism from WNBA fans after appearing to wave goodbye to the Washington Mystics following Atlanta Dream’s playoff-clinching victory on Wednesday night.

Atlanta completed a 2-0 first-round sweep with a 93-75 win in Washington, securing its first semifinal appearance since 2018. Reese played an important role in the victory, finishing with 15 points, seven rebounds, two assists and three blocks while shooting 50% from the field.

Yet the attention quickly shifted from the Dream’s dominant performance to the moments immediately after the final buzzer. Reese and Allisha Gray were seen waving toward the Mystics as Washington’s season came to an end, a gesture that some fans interpreted as taunting the defeated team.

Veteran teammate DeWanna Bonner appeared to step in and stop the moment from going further. The 39-year-old forward was filmed lowering the players’ hands back toward their sides, seemingly signaling that the gesture should end.

Bonner’s intervention drew considerable praise from fans, with many viewing it as an example of veteran leadership and sportsmanship. Some supporters argued that her experience could prove valuable as Atlanta enters the deeper stages of the postseason.

The reaction to Reese , however, was considerably harsher. Several fans described the gesture as “classless” and disrespectful, while others questioned why the players would wave goodbye to an opponent immediately after eliminating them.

The controversy came after Reese had delivered a strong performance in her first WNBA playoff series. She opened the postseason with a double-double before producing a more efficient outing in Game 2. She also helped limit Washington center Shakira Austin to nine points on 3-of-9 shooting.

Reese has previously spoken about the importance of Atlanta controlling its emotions during games, making the post-game incident particularly notable.

“Our memo was to manage emotions better and value possessions more, and that’s what we did the entire time,” Reese said after the victory. “We’ve stayed dialed in all year.”

Reese and Dream now face a tougher semifinal test

Atlanta’s reward for eliminating Washington is a semifinal matchup with the New York Liberty, who swept the Minnesota Lynx in the opening round.

The Liberty could provide a significantly different challenge, particularly because of their combination of size, experience and postseason pedigree. Breanna Stewart and Jonquel Jones give New York a formidable presence around the basket, while Sabrina Ionescu provides another major threat from the perimeter.

Reese has already shown she can make an impact against New York. She recorded 25 points and nine rebounds in a June meeting and later posted 18 points and 10 rebounds during Atlanta’s September victory over the Liberty.

The Dream also won two of their three regular-season meetings with New York, although playoff basketball brings a different level of pressure.

The immediate focus for Reese will now be on helping Atlanta continue its postseason run. The social-media controversy may dominate the conversation temporarily, but the Dream’s next challenge will be decided on the court.

With the Liberty standing between Atlanta and a place in the WNBA Finals, Reese and her teammates won't have much time to dwell on the events following their series-clinching win.

articles.title: Caitlin Clark’s Nike Caitlin 1 launch gives one of her favorite bakeries a surprising new identity
articles.standfirst: A familiar Indianapolis stop and an unusual challenge overseas reveal how fans are joining a milestone that arrives on a pivotal day for Clark
articles.summary: A familiar Indianapolis stop and an unusual challenge overseas reveal how fans are joining a milestone that arrives on a pivotal day for Clark
articles.body:
Open the door, step inside, and a familiar Indianapolis bakery has become part of Caitlin Clark’s story. Long’s Bakery temporarily changed its identity to “Caitlin’s Extraordinary Treats” on October 1, celebrating the global release of the Indiana Fever star’s first signature Nike shoe.

Thousands of miles away, another celebration asks fans to pick up a basketball. Near Nike Fort in the Philippines, the “Caitlin 1 Crane Challenge” features a hoop suspended from a crane. The contrast makes the two clips worth watching together: one brings viewers into a neighborhood business transformed for Clark, while the other invites them to attempt an extraordinary shot of their own.

From an Indianapolis bakery to a hoop suspended from a crane

The bakery walkthrough captures the transformation through the entrance, decorations and displays. For a day, the shop becomes a place where supporters can share in a milestone usually associated with sneaker stores and basketball courts. Local coverage documented Long’s involvement in the launch celebration.

There is a personal connection behind the choice. Long’s Bakery is one of Clark’s favorite spots , making it a fitting place to celebrate a player who has brought new attention to basketball in Indianapolis.

The Philippine activation offers a more physical invitation to participate. Park Access announced the crane challenge at the BHS Activity Center’s Bear Area outside Nike Fort, in Bonifacio Global City, for October 1–4, from 2–6 p.m. daily. Its promotional message challenges visitors to make the shot—a fitting theme for a player known for attempting baskets well beyond the three-point line.

The shoe connecting those celebrations is the Nike Caitlin 1 , which launches globally on October 1 through Nike’s digital platforms and select retailers. Nike lists its North American price at $140 . The release also includes an 18-piece apparel collection, expanding Clark’s debut beyond footwear.

According to Nike, the design centers on the way Clark creates space and changes pace. It combines an Opticast upper with forefoot Air Zoom Turbo cushioning and full-length Cushlon foam. Details incorporating “CC” and “22” connect the performance shoe to her initials and jersey number.

But the celebrations arrive with unfinished business on the court. The Fever kept their season alive with a 99-89 victory over the Aces on September 29. Clark finished with 27 points, 15 assists and seven rebounds, helping Indiana force a third game after its opening defeat.

That deciding first-round game is scheduled for October 1 in Las Vegas. With the best-of-three series tied 1-1, the winner advances to the semifinals. Clark’s global shoe launch and Indiana’s fight to continue its postseason therefore fall on the same day.

The Nike Caitlin 1 launch has given fans plenty to celebrate. Now Clark has a chance to make the day even sweeter on the court. With the series tied 1-1, Indiana faces A’ja Wilson and the Las Vegas Aces in a winner-take-all Game 3 tonight, October 1, at Michelob ULTRA Arena. Tipoff is scheduled for 9 p.m. ET 6 p.m. local time with U.S. coverage on USA Network and CNBC. A victory would send the Fever into the semifinals and keep their championship hopes alive.

articles.title: Enes Kanter urges WNBA to suspend A'ja Wilson after heated playoff exchange with Fever fan
articles.standfirst: WNBA playoff tensions rise after Wilson’s confrontation with a Fever fan
articles.summary: WNBA playoff tensions rise after Wilson’s confrontation with a Fever fan
articles.body:
Former NBA player Enes Kanter Freedom has called on the WNBA to suspend Las Vegas Aces star A’ja Wilson following her heated confrontation with an Indiana Fever fan during Game 2 of the teams’ playoff series.

Kanter took to X on Wednesday, arguing that Wilson should face disciplinary action after leaving the playing area and approaching a spectator near the baseline.

“What a drama queen! A’ja Wilson should be suspended immediately, along with every teammate who followed her into the stands. She left the court, walked into the baseline seats, and confronted a fan,” Kanter wrote on X.

“@WNBA Rule 12A is clear: if a player deliberately enters the stands during a game, they are automatically ejected. The Fever investigated the fan and determined he did NOT violate their Fan Code of Conduct. Hey Aja, You’re the face of the league.

“@WNBA. Control your emotions or face the consequences. Rules are rules. Apply them. #WNBA“

The controversy unfolded during the fourth quarter of Indiana’s 99-89 victory over Las Vegas. Wilson had become tangled with Fever forward Sophie Cunningham , who went down following the play.

As Wilson moved toward the baseline, a fan behind the basket appeared to point in her direction and move toward the court.

Wilson then approached the spectator, pointing and shouting before teammates, coaches and security personnel separated the two. She was assessed a technical foul, while the fan was temporarily removed from his seat.

Wilson explains why she confronted the fan

After the game, Wilson said she believed the fan had stepped toward her while pointing and that his behavior was unacceptable. She acknowledged that the technical foul hurt her team and apologized to her teammates, but stood by her reaction.

“If I see a man come at me, taking steps toward me and pointing at me, I don’t give a damn what you said. I don’t give a damn how you said it, the tone, that is unacceptable,” Wilson said after the game.

“You don’t know me to step toward me and point at me. I’m not for that s**t at all. … That there is unacceptable. How he gets back in the game because they said he didn’t do anything, of course he did.”

The Fever investigated the incident and determined that the spectator hadn't violated the team's Fan Code of Conduct. He was subsequently allowed to return, a decision that Wilson questioned publicly.

Aces coach Becky Hammon defended Wilson , saying she hadn't witnessed the entire exchange but believed her star player had felt deeply disrespected. Hammon also stressed that both players and fans have responsibilities when it comes to conduct inside an arena.

The incident has now created another storyline in an already intense playoff matchup. Sophie Cunningham also appeared to take a jab at Wilson on social media after the confrontation, adding another layer to the growing tension.

Indiana's victory evened the best-of-three series at 1-1 and forced a decisive Game 3 in Las Vegas. Wilson finished Game 2 with 22 points and nine rebounds after producing 38 points and 16 rebounds in the series opener.

Kanter's demand for a suspension has added further attention to the situation, but it appears it’s all for nothing as Wilson is expected to play in Thursday night’s crucial Game 3.

articles.title: Caitlin Clark shoves opponent in heated Game 3 as Fever are knocked out of the playoffs
articles.standfirst: Tension flared just three minutes into Game 3, when Caitlin Clark shoved Brianna Turner after she tried to step into the Fever's huddle.
articles.summary: Tension flared just three minutes into Game 3, when Caitlin Clark shoved Brianna Turner after she tried to step into the Fever's huddle.
articles.body:
Tension was there from the first minute between the Indiana Fever and the Las Vegas Aces on Thursday, in Game 3 of the first round of the playoffs, a win-or-go-home matchup at Michelob ULTRA Arena .

Caitlin Clark has a run-in with Brianna Turner

Just three minutes into the game, Caitlin Clark and Brianna Turner each received a technical foul after a heated exchange. During a stoppage, Turner tried to step into the Fever's huddle and Clark shoved her away.

The intensity was expected in a high-pressure game in which the winner would advance to the semifinals. Clark , known for her competitive streak, didn't want to give the Aces even the slightest edge, while Turner was looking to get into the heads of Indiana's players.

The 24-year-old guard had helped the Fever avoid elimination in Game 2 with a spectacular 27 points , seven rebounds and 15 assists in a 10-point win. It was the first playoff victory of her career.

Coach Stephanie White praised the three-time All-Star, calling her "the engine" of the team, and said she expected Clark to reach "another level" in the decisive Game 3.

Clark's complaint about the officials

Clark also criticized the officiating after Game 2, in which she fouled out with 2:45 left in the fourth quarter.

“I thought the refs really struggled tonight. It's so confusing at times,” said the player, who can do it all on the court.

At the time of this report, Las Vegas led 54-48 at halftime . Clark had 13 points, four assists and two blocks, while A'ja Wilson had 21 points on 7-of-8 shooting from the field and two rebounds.

The Las Vegas Aces won Game 3 to advance to the semifinals, eliminating Caitlin Clark and the Indiana Fever from the WNBA title race.

articles.title: Caitlin Clark suffers bloody face injury after taking hard elbow in Fever-Aces clash
articles.standfirst: Caitlin Clark ended up bloodied after an accidental elbow in the fourth quarter of Game 3.
articles.summary: Caitlin Clark ended up bloodied after an accidental elbow in the fourth quarter of Game 3.
articles.body:
C aitlin Clark of the Indiana Fever ended up with blood on her face after taking a hit during Thursday night's WNBA playoff game against the Las Vegas Aces .

The blow came in the fourth quarter, when Clark went up for a rebound and an Aces player accidentally elbowed her. Indiana's star fell to the floor and stayed down for a few moments before getting up and heading to the tunnel to be checked out.

It looked like she might miss at least a few minutes, but she returned quickly and finished the game.

Fever head coach Stephanie White made her frustration clear that no foul was called. Clark , understandably upset, argued that the play should have been penalized. When she returned to the court, she made sure to show an official the blood coming from her mouth, and the game had to be stopped because she still had blood on her hands.

The play came at a key moment, as the Fever were trying to rally and stay alive in the decisive Game 3.

The Aces eliminate the Fever

The comeback never arrived: the Aces beat Indiana 94-83 and advanced to the next round.

Las Vegas was powered by a legendary performance from center A'ja Wilson, who finished with 36 points on 11-of-18 shooting from the field, plus 10 rebounds.

Clark had a solid start but couldn't sustain it. The Iowa product finished with 18 points on 6-of-18 shooting . Kelsey Mitchell led Indiana's offense with 23 points, and Aliyah Boston added 19.

Now the Fever will have to begin planning for next season, while the Aces wait for the winner of the series between the Dallas Wings and the Golden State Valkyries, which is tied 1-1 and will be decided Friday.

articles.title: Caitlin Clark wakes up to news that could give her career a major boost
articles.standfirst: Clark has added another major milestone to her growing legacy
articles.summary: Clark has added another major milestone to her growing legacy
articles.body:
Caitlin Clark has been doing more than playing basketball and helping change the way women’s sports are viewed. She has also made a major impact from a marketing standpoint, reaching another milestone in her career while continuing to set new standards under the Indiana Fever jersey.

What Clark represents for women’s sports today is significant. Her likeness is often divided, but there is no denying the impact she has had within the league and across women’s sports globally. Now, as she continues to collect personal milestones, Clark woke up to news that could add another important chapter to both her professional career and personal story.

On October 1, Clark added another first to her résumé just hours before taking the court. The Nike Caitlin 1, her first signature basketball shoe, officially launched worldwide, with Nike revealing just how heavily it is backing its newest signature athlete .

During Nike’s fiscal first-quarter earnings call, the company announced that the Caitlin 1 represented the largest women’s signature shoe launch in Nike history. Nike CEO Elliott Hill said the Caitlin 1 would launch in 5,000 stores, twice the average for a Nike Basketball signature shoe, supported by the company’s largest Nike product campaign for the holiday season.

Fans quickly showed their support

The good news arrived early for Clark, as the Caitlin 1 nearly sold out within two hours of its release . Only limited sizes remained through Nike, while several national retailers had already sold out completely.

With the excitement building, Clark also announced that more colorways are on the way, giving fans and collectors another reason to look forward to what comes next for her signature shoe line.

articles.title: Brittany Mahomes shows unwavering WAG support for WNBA by backing Sophie Cunningham
articles.standfirst: Mahomes showed love for the Indiana guard before Game 3
articles.summary: Mahomes showed love for the Indiana guard before Game 3
articles.body:
Brittany Mahomes made clear where her support lay before Sophie Cunningham and the Indiana Fever took the floor for their winner-take-all Game 3 against the Las Vegas Aces .

Cunningham had shared her pregame look from Game 2 on social media, drawing a simple but emphatic response from Mahomes , who posted three fire emojis.

The interaction stood out because Cunningham , a former Missouri star and prominent Kansas City Chiefs fan, has long maintained ties to the region Mahomes represents so visibly.

The show of support came before Indiana’s season came down to one game in Las Vegas. By the time that game was over, however, the conversation surrounding the Fever was much less celebratory.

Elimination came with more officiating frustration

Tension had already been building throughout the series, and Game 3 only added to it.

One of the most controversial sequences came early in the second quarter when Brianna Turner wrapped her arm around Lexie Hull while the two battled for position.

Hull was called for the foul, immediately protested and appeared to signal that she had been pulled to the floor.

Coach Stephanie White attempted to challenge the play, but instead of getting the review she wanted, she was given a technical foul after stepping out of the coach’s box while trying to call timeout.

"They weren't talking to us," White told IndyStar afterward. "They were running away from us, actually, because I got the technical for trying to go on the court to call a timeout to challenge."

The broadcast later indicated that Indiana had missed the replay window. That did little to ease White ’s frustration: "The officiating was terrible," she said after the game.

Cunningham still at center of emotion

White also pointed to the foul disparity, with Las Vegas called for fewer fouls and attempting significantly more free throws than Indiana.

"I'm not trying to say we don't foul, because we do," White said. "I'm saying that other teams do, too. It's a hard pill to swallow when you're not getting the foul calls, when there's not a lot of consistency."

The complaints followed an already emotional Game 2, when A’ja Wilson was assessed a technical foul after confronting a fan. Cunningham later appeared to reference the league’s rules on social media, posting: "according to the rule book…"

That added another layer to a series that had become increasingly personal and physical.

Mahomes ’ reaction to Cunningham came before the deciding game, but it now serves as part of a wider picture of how much attention the Fever guard was drawing heading into Indiana’s final stand.

Cunningham didn't need to score 30 points to become part of the story. Her edge, personality and willingness to speak publicly had already made her one of the more visible figures in the matchup.

Mahomes ’ support only amplified that attention. Indiana’s playoff run is now over, and the Fever leave Las Vegas frustrated by how the final game was officiated.

articles.title: Caitlin Clark makes blunt statement following Fever's painful playoff elimination
articles.standfirst: Clark pointed to a late fourth-quarter review and admitted Indiana never found its best form against Las Vegas
articles.summary: Clark pointed to a late fourth-quarter review and admitted Indiana never found its best form against Las Vegas
articles.body:
The Indiana Fever spent most of Thursday night chasing the Las Vegas Aces , only to pull within one possession late enough to believe a comeback was still there. That is what made the ending so difficult for Caitlin Clark .

Las Vegas eventually closed out a 94-83 win in the deciding WNBA Playoff Game 3, but Clark ’s postgame assessment focused less on the final margin and more on how much Indiana left on the table.

“Just proud of our group for the way we battled and the way we fought,” Clark said. “Things didn’t really go our way tonight. We were right there, and I felt we probably played a ‘C’ game.”

One late sequence changed everything

Indiana trailed 82-80 with just over two minutes remaining when Kelsey Mitchell missed a layup, secured the offensive rebound and went back up. Officials called a foul on Mitchell and awarded possession to Las Vegas.

The Fever challenged the ruling, hoping to keep the ball and potentially tie the game, but the decision stood after review. Clark believed that sequence mattered enormously.

“If the challenge at whatever point that was, with two minutes to go, is called correctly when they go to the monitor, it’s a one-possession game, and we have the ball,” she said.

Las Vegas then created separation, turning a tight finish into a double-digit final margin.

Clark finished with 18 points on 6-of-18 shooting, including 3-of-12 from three-point range, while committing six turnovers. It was not the kind of night she would have wanted with Indiana’s season on the line.

Close without being sharp

That was ultimately Clark ’s point. Indiana hadn't played particularly well, yet the game remained within reach deep into the fourth quarter. The Fever had already shown their resilience by bouncing back from a Game 1 loss to win Game 2 and force the decider.

Thursday gave them another chance to extend their season, but Las Vegas executed better down the stretch. The defeat ended Indiana’s year at 28-16 and sent the Aces through to the semifinals.

Clark ’s comments weren't an attempt to diminish Las Vegas’ performance. They reflected the frustration of knowing Indiana did enough to remain competitive while still making too many mistakes to finish the job.

That may be the hardest part of the loss for the Fever . They weren't blown away from the opening tip. They were still close late, even with Clark struggling from the field and the offense failing to find a consistent rhythm. It wasn't enough to save its season.

articles.title: “I want to feel like I’m dead after the game”: Paige Bueckers ready for the biggest game of her WNBA career in Game 3
articles.standfirst: The winner of Game 3 will advance to the WNBA playoff semifinals to face the Las Vegas Aces
articles.summary: The winner of Game 3 will advance to the WNBA playoff semifinals to face the Las Vegas Aces
articles.body:
The 30th WNBA playoffs have reached a breathtaking climax, with the Atlanta Dream and New York Liberty already locking horns in the semifinals, while the reigning champion Las Vegas Aces anxiously await the winner of the decisive Game 3 showdown between the Dallas Wings and the Golden State Valkyries .

The Wings successfully kept their championship aspirations alive in dramatic fashion, prevailing 108-100 in overtime on Wednesday night behind a historic performance from Arike Ogunbowale , who shattered the WNBA Playoff-record with 45 points , including a miraculous game-tying three-pointer with just 4.1 seconds remaining in regulation.

Dallas now faces the daunting task of replicating that offensive explosion on the road at the Chase Center , where the Valkyries established themselves as a fortress during the regular season by dropping only five home games all year ( 17-5 ).

Paige Bueckers Embraces High Stakes Ahead of Career-Defining Game

After stumbling out of the gate with a heavy 104-80 defeat in Game 1 , where sophomore star Paige Bueckers stood virtually alone as the only Wings player to score more than 11 points, Dallas engineered a resilient bounce-back.

Now, heading into the winner-take-all Game 3 , Bueckers faces the most important fixture of her professional career and is fully prepared to empty the tank.

Reflecting on the physical and emotional toll required to survive elimination, Bueckers told ESPN following Wednesday's thriller at the College Park Center: "I don’t want to actually die out there, but I want to feel like I’m dead after the game."

The star guard emphasized her commitment to putting her body and heart completely on the line to sustain a historic campaign for the No. 7-seeded Wings , whose 27 regular-season victories marked a franchise record and surpassed their combined win total from the previous two seasons.

While Bueckers endured a tougher shooting night in Game 2, chipping in 10 points on 3-of-13 shooting while expertly steering the offensive tempo, she aims to recapture the stellar efficiency from her postseason debut when she poured in 21 points on 90% shooting .

An electric atmosphere awaits in the Bay Area as the Valkyries fight to avoid a heartbreaking opening-round exit for the second straight year, while the surging Wings chase a monumental upset and a semifinal rematch against the Aces.

articles.standfirst: The season ended in Las Vegas, but Caitlin Clark, Sophie Cunningham and Lexie Hull still had one last way to turn heads before saying goodbye to the playoffs.
articles.summary: The season ended in Las Vegas, but Caitlin Clark, Sophie Cunningham and Lexie Hull still had one last way to turn heads before saying goodbye to the playoffs.
articles.body:
Without a doubt, the Indiana Fever’s 2026 season was one of the most important in franchise history. The team finished the regular season with a 28-win record and entered the playoffs with hopes of making a deep run, but their journey came to an end Thursday, October 1, in Las Vegas. After beating the Aces 99-89 at home on September 29, Indiana fell 94-83 in Game 3 and was eliminated after losing the series 2-1 .

But before officially closing the book on their season, Caitlin Clark arrived at the final game with a look ready for a VS alongside Sophie Cunningham and Lexie Hull .

Caitlin Clark took the look in a preppy direction

Clark went with a combination of navy, white and brown that blended a preppy vibe with relaxed tailoring. She wore a slightly cropped navy polo over a white crew-neck T-shirt, letting the white peek through at both the collar and sleeves. The high-waisted, wide-leg navy trousers completed the collegiate feel , while dark brown loafers and a matching leather bag added contrast. Her jewelry was much more understated, with delicate bracelets, small rings and simple earrings.

Sophie Cunningham completely changed the energy

While Clark stuck to a more classic palette, S ophie Cunningham wore white from head to toe. Her look centered around a structured crop top with wide straps and a square neckline , paired with wide-leg white tailored trousers that nearly covered her shoes. Nude pointed-toe heels helped elongate her silhouette, while the outfit kept the overall aesthetic polished and clean. The finishing touch came with a delicate necklace featuring a small crucifix and stud earrings, enough to complete the look without overdoing it.

Lexie Hull went for a resort-inspired look

And if Clark took the VS in a collegiate direction and Sophie went sophisticated, Lexie Hull showed up with a much more relaxed, summery take . The player wore a coordinated cropped top and high-waisted shorts with vertical light blue and white stripes, immediately recalling the aesthetic of a tennis club. White heeled mules and a small matching shoulder bag kept that same feel, while a gold necklace, metallic watch and delicate bracelet completed the outfit.

Who won this round of looks?

articles.title: What happens to Caitlin Clark, Kelsey Mitchell and Sophie Cunningham after the Fever's elimination?
articles.standfirst: Indiana Fever’s season ended in Las Vegas, but while the elimination puts a close to 2026, three of the team’s biggest names are heading into an offseason that could change a lot.
articles.summary: Indiana Fever’s season ended in Las Vegas, but while the elimination puts a close to 2026, three of the team’s biggest names are heading into an offseason that could change a lot.
articles.body:
Indiana Fever certainly started October in a way they did not expect. On Thursday, October 1, the Las Vegas Aces defeated Indiana 94-83 at Michelob ULTRA Arena and ended their season, taking the first-round series 2-1 . The Fever had won 99-89 at home just two days earlier to force a deciding Game 3, but this time, the story was different. The season is over, but a new chapter is beginning, with Caitlin Clark, Kelsey Mitchell and Sophie Cunningham facing three very different scenarios.

Kelsey Mitchell enters free agency at the best moment of her career

Kelsey Mitchell has a very specific reason to look ahead closely: she just put together a huge season.

The guard finished 2026 averaging 24.7 points per game across 44 games, ranking second in scoring across the entire WNBA while shooting 45% from three-point range . She also finished with 1,086 points, breaking the record for the most points scored by an Indiana player in a regular season.

And there is another detail that makes her situation even more interesting: Mitchell is already the Fever’s all-time leading scorer. In April, she signed a one-year, $1.4 million supermax contract , but she has already used the two franchise-player designations allowed. That means that after a season like this, she enters the market as an unrestricted free agent.

That does not mean her story with Indiana is over. It means that, for the first time at this point in her career, what comes next is an open decision.

Sophie Cunningham also has a decision to make

Sophie Cunningham heads into the same offseason from a very different place. The 30-year-old guard did not have Mitchell’s offensive volume, but she found a role that became important for Indiana , especially after returning from a major knee injury.

She played 43 games, including three starts, averaging 7.9 points, 2.3 rebounds and 1.2 assists in 22.2 minutes per game . She also shot 41.9% from three-point range, a number that helped make her a consistent threat off the bench.

Her value also went beyond the numbers. Cunningham brought physical defense, energy and a respected voice in the locker room, elements that do not fully show up in a stat sheet . Now, though, it is time to decide what comes next: her one-year, $665,000 contract expires after this season, making her an unrestricted free agent as well and allowing her to either remain in Indiana or explore other options.

Caitlin Clark is playing a different game off the court

And then there is Caitlin Clark.

Although her name naturally comes up when discussing Indiana’s future, her situation is not the same as Mitchell’s or Cunningham’s. Clark is not entering this offseason as a free agent , but she is the piece around which the franchise will have to continue building its future.

The 24-year-old star finished the regular season averaging 22.3 points and 8.3 assists per game, leading the WNBA in assists. She also helped Indiana reach 28 wins and shared an offense with Mitchell that ranked among the most efficient the league has produced .

And in these playoffs, she delivered another performance that immediately drew attention: 27 points and 15 assists in Game 2, becoming the first player in WNBA playoff history to reach those numbers in the same game. She finished Game 3 with 18 points, but this time, it was not enough to prevent elimination.

articles.title: Caitlin Clark quickly finds new job after Indiana Fever playoff exit
articles.standfirst: The Indiana Fever got eliminated on Thursday, but Clark will get right back to work - kind of - on Saturday.
articles.summary: The Indiana Fever got eliminated on Thursday, but Clark will get right back to work - kind of - on Saturday.
articles.body:
This season was supposed to be a breakout year for Caitlin Clark and the Indiana Fever . Although there were plenty of good moments, the team ended up being seeded against the reigning champions in the playoffs.

A'ja Wilson and the Las Vegas Aces stood in their way. It took all three games, but the Aces came out on top, while Clark struggled in the elimination game . Clark will now probably try to get her mind off of basketball for a little while, and it seems like she's found the perfect side gig to do just that.

Caitlin Clark selected to be guest picker on College GameDay in Iowa

Less than 24 hours after being eliminated from the playoffs, it was announced that Clark is set to be the guest picker on ESPN's College GameDay on Saturday. This one will certainly be a special one for Clark, as she gets to go back to her roots.

GameDay will be hosted in Iowa City , as the featured game is the enticing matchup between the No. 5 Ohio State Buckeyes and No. 14 Iowa Hawkeyes . Clark, of course, played four seasons at Iowa.

It should be a fun show and a nice distraction for Clark to get over the loss to the Aces. Hopefully, the Hawkeyes football team can win and cheer her up even more.

articles.title: Update on Natalie Nakase's Health: How is the Valkyries' coach doing after fainting during an argument with the referee?
articles.standfirst: Golden State Valkyries coach Natalie Nakase briefly collapsed during Friday's playoff win over the Dallas Wings
articles.summary: Golden State Valkyries coach Natalie Nakase briefly collapsed during Friday's playoff win over the Dallas Wings
articles.body:
N atalie Nakase 's health became an unexpected concern during one of the biggest games in Golden State Valkyries history.

The Valkyries defeated the Dallas Wings 77-73 on Friday night to win their first playoff series in franchise history, but the dramatic victory was overshadowed for a period when Nakase suddenly went down near the team's bench late in the fourth quarter.

With 1:40 remaining and Dallas holding a 72-71 lead, Nakase was speaking with an official when she appeared to collapse.

Assistant coaches and members of the team's medical staff immediately moved toward her. Nakase remained on the floor briefly before being helped back to her feet and returning to the sideline.

The 46-year-old coach held her head as she made her way back toward the bench, but she did not leave the game. Instead, she continued directing the Valkyries during the final stretch of a contest that ultimately secured a place in the WNBA semifinals.

The latest update from the team provides some reassurance. The Valkyries told ESPN that Nakase was feeling "exhausted" and "got lightheaded" during the game, but that she was "fine now."

The team also indicated that she was expected to coach Golden State when it begins its semifinal series against the Las Vegas Aces on Sunday.

There has been no public announcement of a specific medical diagnosis or further explanation beyond those comments.

What happened to Natalie Nakase?

Nakase's collapse came during an extremely intense finish to a must-win playoff game for Golden State. The Valkyries had trailed Dallas by as many as 16 points before mounting a fourth-quarter comeback.

After being helped up, Nakase returned to the huddle and continued working with her players. Assistant coach Kasib Powell later emphasized that she remained engaged almost immediately after the incident.

"We're just trying to figure it out," Powell said. "We just know that we've seen her afterwards, and she was fine, laughing, in great spirits. So, you know, I think we'll figure out more as we go. But I think she's totally fine.

"She's talking. She's laughing in the back. So we look forward to preparing and getting ready for Sunday."

Powell added that Nakase was "locked in right after (the incident) happened."

"After the game, we talked to each other, and it was nothing. She didn't miss a beat. I don't know what got her at that moment or exactly what happened, but we do know that she'll be ready to go for Sunday," Powell said.

Golden State star Gabby Williams also offered reassurance when asked about her coach.

"She's fine," Williams said. "We're just happy that she's OK."

Nakase did not participate in the postgame media conference. Powell handled those duties instead, while Nakase was later seen leaving the court with assistance from a member of the coaching staff.

Her brief absence from the podium, combined with the footage of her collapse, naturally prompted concern, but the available information does not indicate a more serious diagnosis.

The team has publicly described the episode in terms of exhaustion and lightheadedness and has said Nakase was feeling fine afterward.

The timing of the incident was particularly remarkable because Golden State still needed its coach during the closing seconds.

With the game hanging in the balance, Nakase remained involved and later successfully challenged a late ruling involving Gabby Williams . The Valkyries held on for the four-point victory, completing a comeback from a 16-point deficit and advancing to the semifinals.

The next challenge arrives quickly. Golden State, the No. 2 seed, will host the No. 3 seed Las Vegas Aces in Game 1 of the best-of-five semifinal series at Chase Center on Sunday, October 4, at 1 p.m. local time.

For now, the most recent public update is that Nakase is expected to be there. The Valkyries have not disclosed additional medical details, so any further conclusions about what caused the episode would go beyond what the team has confirmed.

For a coach who remained on the sideline through the final minutes of a historic playoff victory, the immediate message from Golden State has been consistent: Nakase is fine and preparing to continue leading the Valkyries.

articles.title: Paige Bueckers breaks her fans' hearts: the Dallas star breaks down after losing to the Valkyries
articles.standfirst: Paige Bueckers struggled to contain her emotions after the Dallas Wings' season ended with a 77-73 loss to the Golden State Valkyries despite a 16-point lead
articles.summary: Paige Bueckers struggled to contain her emotions after the Dallas Wings' season ended with a 77-73 loss to the Golden State Valkyries despite a 16-point lead
articles.body:
P aige Bueckers ' second WNBA season ended in heartbreaking fashion, and the Dallas Wings star struggled to hide her emotions after the team's playoff elimination Friday night.

Dallas was within touching distance of the WNBA semifinals after building a 16-point advantage against the Golden State Valkyries in Game 3 of their first-round series.

Instead, the Wings watched that lead disappear as Golden State completed a dramatic comeback and secured a 77-73 victory.

The result ended Dallas ' season and sent the Valkyries into the semifinals, where they will face the Las Vegas Aces . For Bueckers , the defeat was particularly difficult after she had helped establish Dallas as a playoff team during her second professional campaign.

Bueckers was visibly emotional during her postgame press conference. The 25-year-old guard had just played 38 minutes in an elimination game and finished with 17 points, six assists, two steals and two blocks.

However, she struggled to find her shooting rhythm, going 3-for-14 from the field and 1-for-4 from three-point range.

She also went scoreless in the fourth quarter as Golden State 's defense increasingly made it difficult for her to create clean opportunities.

The Valkyries used several defenders to make Bueckers work throughout the deciding game.

Kaila Charles, Tiffany Hayes and Gabby Williams were among those involved in limiting Dallas' leading scorer, with the defensive pressure becoming increasingly important as Golden State erased the Wings' advantage.

Dallas entered halftime with a 44-37 lead and then appeared to take control when the margin grew to 53-37 early in the third quarter. But the Valkyries gradually chipped away at the deficit.

Golden State eventually tied the contest at 65 before taking control in the closing minutes. Gabby Williams became particularly influential down the stretch, while the Valkyries' defense prevented Dallas from finding the offensive consistency it needed.

Bueckers' playoff disappointment does not erase her season

Arike Ogunbowale gave Dallas everything she had in the elimination game, scoring 30 points and grabbing five rebounds. But the Wings could not convert their advantage into a series victory.

For Bueckers , the final two games of the series represented a difficult contrast with the beginning of her postseason. She opened the playoffs with 21 points on 9-of-10 shooting in Game 1, showing why she had become such a central part of Dallas' future.

The Valkyries adjusted defensively afterward, holding her to 10 points on 3-of-13 shooting in Game 2 before Friday's 17-point performance.

That late-series struggle, however, came after a regular season in which Bueckers took another major step forward.

She averaged 20.9 points, 5.9 assists and 4.1 rebounds per game while shooting 51.2% from the field, 41% from three-point range and 87.1% from the free-throw line. The WNBA's official player profile confirms those numbers for her 2026 campaign.

Those statistics followed an impressive rookie year in which Bueckers won Rookie of the Year and earned All-WNBA Second Team honors. She was also selected to the All-Star team during her first professional season.

Dallas head coach Jose Fernandez defended Bueckers after the elimination, emphasizing how much responsibility she carried during the season.

"Paige is taking it hard," Fernandez said after Game 3. "She carries that load. She's a winner. This series shouldn't have any inkling on the kind of season she had for us. We don't get to this point without Paige. She takes a lot of ownership and carries a heavy load. The great ones do."

The Wings' elimination also marks the end of Bueckers ' first WNBA playoff series. While the conclusion was painful, Dallas' postseason appearance represented another step in the development of a young franchise built around its No. 1 overall pick from the 2025 draft.

For now, Bueckers and the Wings are left to reflect on a series that slipped away after they had Golden State on the ropes.

The Valkyries move forward to face Las Vegas, while Bueckers enters the offseason after another statistically significant season, one that ended with disappointment, but also reinforced her importance to Dallas' long-term ambitions.

articles.body:
The Indiana Fever 's 2026 season ended with another loss to the Las Vegas Aces , but the biggest questions facing the franchise now extend beyond the scoreboard.

There has been no announcement that White is being fired. However, the nature of Indiana's elimination inevitably raises questions about whether the organization believes a different coach could take its talented core further.

The Fever finished 28-16 during the regular season, their best record in 14 years, but a 4-4 finish left them sixth in the standings and facing a formidable first-round opponent.

They managed to force a deciding game against Las Vegas after winning Game 2, only to see their season end in Nevada.

That result is particularly difficult to evaluate because Indiana had three established offensive pillars in Clark, Mitchell and Aliyah Boston .

Clark enjoyed the best scoring season of her WNBA career, averaging 22.3 points per game, while Mitchell established a league record with 27 consecutive games scoring at least 20 points. Boston also remained one of the team's central pieces.

Yet the Fever still finished sixth and could not advance beyond the opening round.

Why Caitlin Clark could be central to Indiana's coaching decision

The question facing Indiana is not simply whether White produced a good regular season. It is whether she produced enough with a roster that contains some of the league's most recognizable talent.

That evaluation becomes even more complicated because Clark's relationship with White reportedly remains strong despite several highly visible moments of disagreement between the coach and star guard.

Clark's long-term situation also matters. While there is no confirmed indication that she is leaving Indiana, any uncertainty surrounding the franchise's direction will inevitably be viewed through the lens of its most important player.

The Fever have built their future around Clark, and the organization will want to ensure that its coaching structure gives her the best opportunity to compete for championships. Indiana's official postgame coverage following the elimination continued to feature both Clark and White , with no indication of an immediate coaching change.

White has nevertheless acknowledged the extraordinary pressure that comes with coaching Indiana.

"There's an infatuation with our team, and there's an infatuation with some of our players, and there's a lot of negativity that surrounds anything that's different from what the fandom wants to see," White said to ESPN for a Sept. 25 story. "And that is challenging as a coach to navigate."

The pressure has only intensified around Clark , whose popularity has transformed the Fever into one of the WNBA's most closely followed teams.

At the same time, there is a strong argument for retaining White .

She has a 52-36 regular-season record across her two seasons since returning to Indiana and helped the Fever reach the semifinals in 2025, their deepest postseason run in 11 years. That team reached the final four despite Clark missing significant time because of injury before eventually losing an overtime Game 5 to the Aces.

White also entered Indiana with considerable coaching credibility. She won the 2023 WNBA Coach of the Year award with Connecticut and went 55-25 during her two seasons with the Sun.

Her earlier stint with Indiana was successful as well. From 2015-16, she went 37-31 and guided the Fever to the WNBA Finals in 2015. Including her Connecticut tenure, White's WNBA head-coaching record stands at 144-92, a .610 winning percentage.

Those achievements make an immediate dismissal far from an obvious decision.

There is also the personal connection. White is Indiana basketball royalty, having been named Indiana Miss Basketball and Gatorade Player of the Year at Seeger High School before becoming a consensus All-American at Purdue and helping the Boilermakers win their first NCAA championship in 1999.

The financial side of the decision is unclear, too. The length and financial terms of the contract White signed in 2024 have not been publicly disclosed, including whether Indiana would owe a buyout if it decided to make a change.

The Fever also have precedent for making a coaching change after two seasons. Christie Sides , White's predecessor, was fired in 2024 after her second season despite having signed a four-year contract.

For now, however, White remains the Fever's coach. The latest official team coverage includes her alongside Clark following the playoff elimination, and no firing has been announced.

Indiana's offseason will therefore be about more than finding answers to one question. The franchise must determine how to strengthen its supporting cast, preserve its relationship with Clark and decide whether White is the coach capable of turning a promising regular-season team into a genuine championship contender.

The 2026 season showed that the Fever can win consistently. Their next decision will determine whether the organization believes White is the person to take that progress one step further.

articles.summary: The Golden State Valkyries survived one of the wildest games in their young franchise history Friday night.
articles.body:
The Golden State Valkyries survived one of the wildest games in their young franchise history Friday night.

But their dramatic 77-73 victory over the Dallas Wings was briefly overshadowed by a frightening moment involving head coach Natalie Nakase.

With roughly 1:40 remaining in the fourth quarter of the decisive Game 3 of the WNBA playoffs, Nakase was speaking with a referee near the Valkyries' bench when she suddenly went down to her hands and knees.

Athletic trainer Katelin Knox and members of the coaching staff immediately moved toward her and helped her back to her feet.

articles.title: Sophie Cunningham finds out what the Indiana Fever GM said about her future in Indiana
articles.standfirst: Like Kelsey Mitchell, Cunningham will be a free agent and may leave the Indiana Fever
articles.summary: Like Kelsey Mitchell, Cunningham will be a free agent and may leave the Indiana Fever
articles.body:
The 30th WNBA semifinals are set, with one series between the Atlanta Dream and New York Liberty and the other pitting the Golden State Valkyries against the reigning champions, the Las Vegas Aces .

The Aces advanced after eliminating the Indiana Fever for a second straight season in an elimination game, and they are now chasing a fourth title in five seasons with future five-time MVP A’ja Wilson leading the way.

For teams like the Dallas Wings and Indiana Fever, the offseason starts now. Both clubs have young franchise pieces, Caitlin Clark and Paige Bueckers , with the talent to win if the roster around them keeps improving.

Fever GM Amber Cox addresses Cunningham’s free agency future

Indiana Fever general manager Amber Cox was direct when asked whether Sophie Cunningham’s off-court profile would shape how the franchise handles her free agency.

Cunningham is set to hit the open market this winter after two seasons in Indianapolis, the last of them on a one-year deal.

On the floor she remained a useful shooter off the bench. In 43 regular-season games she averaged 7.9 points, 2.3 rebounds and 1.2 assists in 22.2 minutes, hitting 46.0 percent from the field and 41.9 percent from three on 3.7 attempts a night (67 of 160).

In the three-game first-round series she put up 7.3 points and shot 44.4 percent from deep . Judging her production is straightforward.

The harder question for front offices is the noise that follows her. Cunningham draws attention for comments that travel well beyond the locker room , and some of that attention has landed awkwardly for a team still trying to turn a record offense into a longer playoff run. Cox shut that door.

Asked if any of the outside “stuff” would change how she evaluates Cunningham, she answered “No.” She then pointed to two productive years as a shooter, called her a steady voice in the locker room and a connector who brings both experience and levity, and said the Fever look forward to those talks. “She had a really productive year, and we’ll see just where things take us,” Cox said.

Openness from the front office does not lock Cunningham into a Fever jersey for 2027. Her situation is one of several decisions Indiana has to make, starting with Kelsey Mitchell after an MVP-caliber season in which she averaged 24.7 points and scored 1,086 (WNBA record) in 44 games .

Cunningham’s shooting and locker-room role give Indiana a reason to stay in the mix. Whether that interest survives a market that will have other options is the part Cox left open.

articles.title: Sophie Cunningham isn’t holding back on A’ja Wilson after fan incident
articles.standfirst: The Indiana guard says players can’t demand more fans while taking issue with ordinary reactions from spectators
articles.summary: The Indiana guard says players can’t demand more fans while taking issue with ordinary reactions from spectators
articles.body:
Sophie Cunningham has reignited the controversy surrounding A’ja Wilson’s confrontation with a fan, arguing that the WNBA applied a “double standard” by choosing not to impose additional discipline on the Las Vegas Aces star.

The incident happened during Game 2 of the Aces’ first-round playoff series against the Indiana Fever. With just over four minutes remaining, Cunningham was called for a foul on Wilson .

A fan behind the baseline then stood up and pointed toward Wilson , prompting the four-time MVP to approach him and exchange words.

Several Aces players moved in to separate Wilson from the spectator, while officials assessed her a technical foul. The fan was escorted from the area but was later permitted to return to his seat after the Fever determined that he hadn’t violated the team’s fan code of conduct.

The WNBA subsequently reviewed the incident and decided Wilson wouldn’t face any additional punishment. League officials determined that she remained in the player escape lane adjacent to the court rather than entering the stands. Two Aces players who left the bench area during the incident also avoided further discipline.

Cunningham believes the league could’ve handled the situation differently. Speaking on her “No Hesitation” podcast, she compared Wilson’s position in the WNBA to LeBron James’ status in the NBA and suggested that the league’s treatment of its biggest stars can create a different standard.

"She's like the LeBron James of our league, and so of course they're not going to suspend her... Something should have happened," Cunningham said.

"The two people who came off the bench onto the court, that should have happened. I think there's definitely a double standard."

Cunningham tells Wilson to “grow up”

Cunningham went beyond questioning the league’s decision and directly criticized Wilson’s reaction to the fan. She argued that players need to accept a certain amount of interaction from spectators, particularly as the WNBA continues to attract new audiences.

"We yell from the rooftops that we want equality, that we want to be treated like the men, that we want all this stuff and we deserve all these things, and we do, we do deserve it," Cunningham said.

"But if you're asking for all these fans to come— and you have new fans, who are real sports fans, and they come and do something that a sports fan would probably do if you're on the opposing team, and then you're going to go for him for just pointing, saying that you fouled? Grow up."

Cunningham also pointed to the criticism she received throughout the season as a reason she felt comfortable making the comments.

“I can say that because I got [expletive] on the entire season. People came after who I am, my character, what I stand for. I’ve heard the worst of the worst. It’s part of it. Who cares?”

Wilson , meanwhile, maintained after Game 2 that the fan’s behavior was unacceptable because he had pointed toward her and stepped in her direction. She apologized to her teammates for receiving the technical foul.

The controversy didn’t affect Wilson’s performance in the deciding game. She responded with 36 points and 10 rebounds as Las Vegas defeated Indiana 94-83, ending the Fever’s playoff run and advancing to the semifinals.

articles.title: Caitlin Clark drops blunt verdict after Fever’s season comes to an end
articles.standfirst: The Fever star offered an honest assessment of Indiana’s elimination before quickly returning to the spotlight in Iowa City
articles.summary: The Fever star offered an honest assessment of Indiana’s elimination before quickly returning to the spotlight in Iowa City
articles.body:
Caitlin Clark didn’t sugarcoat the Indiana Fever’s latest playoff disappointment, but her comments after elimination also revealed a player already looking ahead.

Indiana’s season came to an end Thursday night with a 94-83 loss to the defending WNBA champion Las Vegas Aces in Game 3 of their first-round playoff series. The result marked the second straight season in which Las Vegas eliminated Indiana from the postseason.

A’ja Wilson once again proved difficult to contain, leading all scorers with 36 points while grabbing 10 rebounds. Chelsea Gray contributed 23 points, and Jackie Young finished with 18 points, eight rebounds and seven assists.

The Fever received 23 points from Kelsey Mitchell , while Aliyah Boston posted 19 points and 10 rebounds. Clark added 18 points, four assists, four blocks and two steals as Indiana attempted to keep pace with the defending champions.

Despite the defeat, Clark didn’t view the game as one in which the Fever were completely outclassed.

“We were right there, and I feel like we played a ‘C’ game,” Clark said after the loss.

Clark believes the Fever had left opportunities on the table because even without playing their best basketball, Indiana remained within striking distance before Las Vegas eventually pulled away.

Clark’s postgame comments also focused on a much bigger picture, as after missing significant time the previous season, she described 2026 as the most basketball she’s played in a single year of her career.

The 24-year-old explained that she hadn’t really taken an extended break after the previous WNBA campaign, instead moving into USA Basketball commitments and preparation for the new season. She acknowledged the workload but also emphasized how rewarding the process had been.

“This is like obviously the most basketball I’ve played at any year of my career,” Clark said.

“And to be completely honest with you, I didn’t take a break when our season ended last year.

So I’ve been going for almost what a year and a half or whatever it is now because I had to prepare for USA Basketball in December and then March and getting ready for our season.

Clark quickly turns the page

Clark said the work she put in during the offseason translated into her strongest season and helped her improve across multiple areas. At the same time, she made it clear that she doesn’t believe her development is finished.

“I love the work. I love being in the gym,” Clark said, but that break didn’t keep her away from the basketball spotlight for long.

On Saturday, Clark returned to Iowa City as ESPN’s College GameDay guest picker before Iowa’s matchup with Ohio State. The former Hawkeye received a huge welcome from the home crowd and also celebrated the release of her first signature Nike basketball shoe.

Clark tossed signed pairs of the Nike Caitlin 1 into the crowd, giving several Iowa fans a memorable souvenir.

The shoe officially launched globally on October 1 and was created around three performance goals identified by Clark : a quicker first step, a faster step-back and a quicker release.

Nike says the Caitlin 1 features its Opticast upper, a forefoot Air Zoom Turbo unit and full-length Cushlon foam. The shoe launched at $140 in North America.

articles.standfirst: Behind the Caitlin 1 launch were more than two years of work, carefully crafted details and a team fans rarely get to see
articles.summary: Behind the Caitlin 1 launch were more than two years of work, carefully crafted details and a team fans rarely get to see
articles.body:
C aitlin Clark’s first signature Nike shoe sold out in minutes , according to a behind-the-scenes post celebrating its release. But the detail that makes the story more interesting is how long it took to reach that moment: more than two years, countless hours and even design work done on a plane using a laptop trackpad.

Its author describes the care poured into every “CC” and every “22,” right down to the edges. Nike’s campaign says “Nothing Special To See Here.” The post offers a different perspective: there was something special in the work fans never saw.

Two years of work behind a $140 shoe

Released October 1, the adult Caitlin 1 retails for $140 . It features Clark’s initials and jersey number, an Opticast upper designed to support quick lateral movement, a forefoot Air Zoom Turbo unit and full-length Cushlon cushioning. The launch included the blue “Caitlin Blue” and yellow “Warning Code” editions.

Clark’s Indiana Fever teammates were among the first to receive the Caitlin 1 before its public release. articles.title: What is the WNBA's "EPIC" extension and why is Caitlin Clark set to get one before 2027 season?
articles.standfirst: Clark's strong start to her WNBA career is set to earn her a big pay bump before her rookie contract expires.
articles.summary: Clark's strong start to her WNBA career is set to earn her a big pay bump before her rookie contract expires.
articles.body:
The 2026 season for the Indiana Fever wasn't quite the breakout one that Caitlin Clark and the team envisioned. The Fever were a solid playoff team, and Clark once again made the All-Star team, but both leave the season feeling disappointed.

Clark didn't take the epic, MVP-level leap many fans expected to see. Her scoring output and efficiency went up, and she limited her turnovers much better, so there are real signs of optimism that the true breakout is coming in 2027 . Next season just so happens to be the final year of her rookie contract, too.

With that in mind, the Fever would love to be able to build around Clark before they have to give her a big contract extension after the 2027 season. But they won't have as much cap space flexibility as expected, because Clark is set to get a big pay raise this offseason .

Caitlin Clark is eligible for a big money EPIC extension in 2027

Clark has earned the right to sign an EPIC extension , a provision created by the WNBA to make it easier for outstanding young players to earn a max or supermax extension ahead of their fourth season. In order to quality for the EPIC extension, a player must earn All-WNBA or MVP honors within their first three years in the league.

Clark earned All-WNBA First Team honors as a rookie in 2024 . That will now allow her to renegotiate her salary for the 2027 season up to the standard max . The Fever would be wise to get her extended this offseason regardless.

articles.title: The Indiana Fever's general manager sends a message to the WNBA about Caitlin Clark that might not go over well
articles.standfirst: Amber Cox has urged the WNBA to recognize Caitlin Clark's influence after another disappointing playoff exit for Indiana
articles.summary: Amber Cox has urged the WNBA to recognize Caitlin Clark's influence after another disappointing playoff exit for Indiana
articles.body:
The Indiana Fever 's 2026 season ended earlier than they would have wanted, but general manager Amber Cox does not believe that should overshadow what Caitlin Clark has done for the franchise and the WNBA .

Following Indiana's first-round playoff elimination by the Las Vegas Aces , Cox delivered an emphatic assessment of Clark's importance to the league.

Her message was unmistakable: the WNBA has benefited enormously from Clark's arrival, and Cox believes that contribution should be acknowledged more openly.

“What she has meant to our team, what she has meant to the league and what she’s meant to women’s basketball. She remains the tipping point,” Cox said of Clark on Saturday.

“You look at the ratings and you look at the full buildings, you know that started in 2024 when she came into the league. And that’s because of Caitlin Clark .”

That is a particularly notable statement from an executive because Clark's impact has frequently been debated alongside the performances of the league's other stars.

Cox was careful to make clear that recognizing Clark does not mean diminishing what came before her: “That does not take anything away from anybody who’s come before her or still playing or has worked in the league. … The build was slow, and then Caitlin Clark arrived and the floodgates opened.”

There is substantial evidence behind the broader point. The WNBA experienced a significant attendance increase during Clark's rookie season in 2024. League-wide attendance reached 2.35 million, its highest total in 22 years, while the average crowd rose 48% from the previous season.

Indiana's home attendance also established a new franchise record, with the Fever drawing 340,715 fans.

The growth has continued beyond Clark's first season. According to data cited by Front Office Sports, the WNBA drew a record 3.79 million fans across 330 games in 2026, averaging 11,474 per game. Fever games were also the most-watched across the league's broadcast partners.

Those numbers provide context for why Cox is so forceful in her praise.

Clark's influence is clear, but Indiana still needs results

The difficulty for the Fever is that commercial growth and basketball success are not the same thing.

Indiana has now failed to reach the semifinals in two consecutive seasons after making the final four in 2025. The Fever went 28-16 during the 2026 regular season, but the No. 6 seed was eliminated by Las Vegas in three games.

The deciding contest ended 94-83, with A'ja Wilson producing 36 points and 10 rebounds for the Aces. Clark finished with 18 points, four assists, two rebounds, two steals and four blocks.

That result inevitably shifts attention toward what Indiana needs to change.

Clark herself had an excellent comeback campaign after appearing in only 13 games during an injury-hit 2025 season. She averaged 22.3 points and 8.3 assists in 2026 while shooting 44.6% from the field and 36.1% from three-point range. She also earned Comeback Player of the Year recognition.

Cox was particularly complimentary of Clark's development, saying she had taken another step as a mid-range scorer and finisher while also improving defensively. The Fever's challenge is now turning that individual production into deeper playoff runs.

Cox's comments also arrive as Indiana enters an important offseason. Kelsey Mitchell , who averaged 24.7 points during the regular season and set a WNBA record with 1,086 points, is an unrestricted free agent.

The franchise also has roster decisions to make around Clark , Aliyah Boston and the rest of its core.

That makes the GM's comments about Clark particularly relevant.

“Obviously, the WNBA is incredibly fortunate. Everybody has benefited thanks to her, and so we all need to say thank you more often,” Cox added.

The statement is unlikely to be universally welcomed, particularly by those who believe the league's growth should be attributed to decades of work by players, executives and fans rather than one individual.

Cox anticipated that criticism, however, by explicitly acknowledging the contribution of those who came before Clark . Her argument is instead about acceleration.

The WNBA had already been growing before 2024, but Clark's arrival coincided with a dramatic increase in attention, attendance and television audiences. That makes her role in the league's current commercial landscape difficult to dismiss.

Still, the Fever cannot afford to make the conversation exclusively about those numbers.

Clark's presence has helped put Indiana at the center of the WNBA, but the franchise's ultimate objective remains winning.

The Aces have now eliminated the Fever in consecutive postseasons, and Indiana will need to address its roster and defensive shortcomings if it wants Clark's next playoff appearance to last longer. Cox's message, therefore, serves two purposes.

It is a defense of the franchise player and an acknowledgment of what Clark has done for the league. But it is also a reminder to the WNBA that the attention surrounding its biggest young star has tangible value.

Whether everyone agrees with Cox's wording or not, the numbers make one part of her argument difficult to ignore. Caitlin Clark has changed the scale of attention surrounding the WNBA.

Now the Fever have to make sure that increased attention is accompanied by increased success on the court.

articles.title: Caitlin Clark's Nike Caitlin 1 sneakers work “magic” with Pat McAfee after she debuted them at home
articles.standfirst: Caitlin Clark's first signature shoe has officially arrived, and Pat McAfee's playful reaction provided another memorable moment during her return to Iowa City
articles.summary: Caitlin Clark's first signature shoe has officially arrived, and Pat McAfee's playful reaction provided another memorable moment during her return to Iowa City
articles.body:
C aitlin Clark may have seen her WNBA season come to an earlier end than she wanted, but the Indiana Fever star has wasted little time finding another way to make headlines.

Clark returned to Iowa City on Saturday as a guest picker on ESPN's College GameDay, appearing alongside Pat McAfee and the rest of the show's crew before Iowa hosted Ohio State.

The former Hawkeye was back in familiar surroundings just days after Indiana was eliminated from the WNBA playoffs by the Las Vegas Aces .

Rather than simply talk college football, Clark also used the opportunity to showcase something that has been years in the making: her first signature basketball shoe with Nike.

The Nike Caitlin 1 officially launched globally on October 1, making the College GameDay appearance one of Clark's first major public opportunities to promote the sneakers following their release.

Nike describes the shoe as being designed around the qualities that define Clark's game, including her speed, shooting range and ability to change direction unpredictably.

Clark arrived in Iowa City wearing a sparkling version of the sneakers and encouraged fans to check them out. Her message was partly promotional and partly a joke directed toward McAfee , who had already tried a pair himself.

“Come on!.. I brought super sparkly… Pat said they’re even super comfortable, even if you don’t play ball, go get them,” Clark said during the segment.

McAfee had apparently already conducted his own test.

The former NFL punter revealed that he had worn the Caitlin 1s the previous night and was impressed by how they felt. His assessment became particularly entertaining when he connected the footwear to his performance on a basketball court.

“I have fat feet. I wore them last night. They were comfortable. I went down to the basketball court down there and got absolutely wet from the logo,” McAfee said during the segment.

The exchange gave Clark an easy way to highlight one of the selling points of the shoe beyond its connection to her basketball career: comfort.

Caitlin Clark has been building anticipation for the Caitlin 1

The timing of the College GameDay appearance is significant because the Caitlin 1 is no longer simply an upcoming product. It is now available to consumers, with Nike listing the shoe in the UK at £129.99, while the U.S. launch price is $140.

Nike's design places considerable emphasis on Clark's playing style. The shoe uses an Opticast upper designed to provide lightweight support, while a forefoot Air Zoom Turbo unit and Cushlon foam are intended to provide responsive cushioning.

The design also includes Clark -specific touches such as her CC logo, references to her No. 22 jersey and stacked Swoosh detailing.

Clark has also been promoting the sneakers in a much more personal way.

Before the public release, she gave pairs to her Fever teammates, turning the locker room into something of an unofficial preview for the product.

After Indiana defeated the Dallas Wings in August, Clark surprised teammates with Nike shoes that included unreleased Caitlin 1s. Tyasha Harris captured the excitement on social media, writing that “Christmas came early.”

She repeated the gesture following Team USA's gold-medal run at the FIBA Women's World Cup in September, handing out unreleased Racer Blue versions when she returned to the Fever locker room.

Makayla Timpson 's reaction became one of the memorable moments from the videos shared online: “Going global in these shoes.”

Those moments have helped create interest around the Caitlin 1 without relying exclusively on traditional advertising. Having Clark's teammates receive and react to the shoes gives fans a glimpse of the product in a genuine basketball environment.

That is particularly useful for a first signature shoe, because the Caitlin 1 is more than another piece of Clark merchandise.

It represents a significant milestone in her relationship with Nike and places her among a relatively small group of active basketball players with their own signature footwear.

The release also comes at an interesting point in Clark's career.

Her 2026 WNBA season ended in the first round when the Fever fell 94-83 to the Aces in Game 3. Clark finished that game with 18 points, while A'ja Wilson produced 36 points and 10 rebounds to send Las Vegas through to the semifinals.

Yet the end of Indiana's campaign has not stopped Clark's momentum away from the court. Her College GameDay appearance brought her back to the place where her national profile first exploded, while the launch of the Caitlin 1 gives her another major platform outside the WNBA.

And McAfee's reaction only added to the fun.

Whether the Caitlin 1 can become a long-term success will ultimately depend on how basketball players respond to it, but Clark has already given Nike plenty of attention around its launch.

For now, her playful exchange with McAfee has provided another piece of publicity for a shoe that is designed to reflect exactly how Clark wants her game to be remembered: fast, confident and willing to shoot from anywhere.

articles.standfirst: Dream host Liberty in a Semifinal showdown as Atlanta looks to finish what September Started
articles.summary: Dream host Liberty in a Semifinal showdown as Atlanta looks to finish what September Started
articles.body:
The WNBA Playoffs have reached their defining stretch, and few matchups carry the weight of what unfolds at Gateway Center Arena when the Atlanta Dream welcome the New York Liberty.

Two of the Eastern Conference's standard-bearers arrive riding momentum from first-round sweeps, and the familiarity between them is anything but incidental — these clubs met twice in the final week of the regular season, and both of those meetings went Atlanta's way.

Atlanta Dream vs New York Liberty: Schedule and where to watch game 1

Tip-off for the Atlanta Dream vs New York Liberty game 1 is set for Sunday, October 4, 2026, at 1:00 p.m. Eastern Time (12:00 p.m. Central Time and 10:00 a.m. Pacific Time), at Gateway Center Arena in Atlanta , a compact 3,500-seat venue that should be loud from the opening possession.

You can catch the action across the WNBA Playoffs on different networks; and for this particular semifinals game you’ll be able to watch it on ESPN and fubo, DirecTV and the ESPN app on streaming.

How do Atlanta Dream and New York Liberty got here

Atlanta enters as the hotter team and the higher seed. The Dream finished atop the Eastern Conference at 30-14 , fourth overall in the league, and have barely broken stride since. They dispatched the Washington Mystics in their opening playoff series, winning 92-77 at home and then closing it out 93-75 on the road.
