articles.title: Kelsey Mitchell reveals problems with Indiana Fever and may leave because of Caitlin Clark
articles.standfirst: Mitchell is entering unrestricted free agency after another impressive season in Indiana
articles.summary: Mitchell is entering unrestricted free agency after another impressive season in Indiana
articles.body:
K elsey Mitchell 's future with the Indiana Fever has suddenly become one of the biggest questions of the WNBA offseason, and her latest comments have offered an unusually candid look at what it is like to play alongside Caitlin Clark .

Mitchell has spent her entire WNBA career in Indiana after being selected No.2 overall in the 2018 draft.

For years, she was the centerpiece of a struggling franchise, carrying much of the offensive responsibility before the Fever eventually landed Aliyah Boston and Clark with consecutive No.1 picks. Now, however, the 30-year-old guard is an unrestricted free agent.

Her comments following Indiana's playoff elimination suggested that her decision will involve much more than money or basketball.

“Showing up every day to compete for fans that may or may not like you is hard. I don’t think people understand that,” Mitchell said at the Fever's end-of-season press conference.

She then explained how playing alongside Clark has brought an additional layer of attention to every member of the Indiana roster.

“I think having to show up for people that don’t look at you and have, you know, the star eyes when they see me," Mitchell said. "But playing with CC and having the eyes that she got, we get a lot of flak just for being on her team.

"So I think that comes with a lot too, and I think that people gotta give us grace. I think that this organization is unbelievable, man, but I think that when it comes to really trying to be yourself, it hasn’t always been easy. That’s all I’ll say."

Mitchell 's remarks may not amount to a declaration that she wants to leave the Fever. In fact, she has repeatedly spoken positively about the organization and her teammates.

But they do demonstrate that the enormous attention surrounding Clark has affected the wider group.

Free agency decision comes after career-best season

The timing is particularly significant because Mitchell has arguably never been more valuable to Indiana.

She averaged 24.7 points per game during the 2026 regular season, shooting 50.9% from the field and 45.0% from three-point range. She played all 44 regular-season games and became one of the league's most productive offensive players.

Her postseason performances were strong, too. Mitchell scored 26 points in Indiana's 99-89 Game 2 victory over Las Vegas to force a decisive matchup, before leading the Fever again with 23 points in the season-ending 94-83 defeat.

The Fever ultimately lost the first-round series 2-1, ending a season in which Indiana finished 28-16 and earned the No.6 seed. That means Mitchell heads into free agency with significant leverage.

She has also made it clear that she intends to consider what is best for her rather than automatically returning to the franchise where she has spent nine seasons.

“I think I have to be selfish. I think that’s where I am in my career, about what I probably need and what's probably best for me," Mitchell said.

“I've got to be selfish where my career is going, in terms of what's important to me. Whether it be winning, whether it be my own individual success.

"I worked my tail off to be here, so whatever I do, it's gonna come from a selfish standpoint. I'll be honest about that.”

Fever general manager Amber Cox has made no secret of the organization's desire to retain Mitchell, saying that the team hopes to keep her in Indiana for the remainder of her career.

“I mean, Kelsey is obviously a major priority. She has a lot of equity in this franchise and has put in a lot of time,” Cox said. She also indicared the Fever hope to build on the partnership between Mitchell and Clark .

The difficulty is that Mitchell 's concerns go beyond basketball. The Fever have been surrounded by controversy throughout the season, with incidents involving fans, opposing players and social-media criticism repeatedly becoming part of the conversation.

During the playoffs, A'ja Wilson confronted a fan during Game 2, while other incidents involving Fever games had already generated significant attention. Mitchell said the online side of the experience has been particularly difficult.

“I don’t think people really understand how much we endured,” she added. “If I showed y’all my DMs about the hate and all of the stuff that comes with being a professional athlete but specifically being an Indiana Fever basketball player, it’s a lot that goes into that.”

Those comments stand in contrast with Cox 's defense of the Fever fanbase. The general manager said that “attacks on our fan base have no basis in reality,” creating an obvious difference in how the experience is being perceived by the players and the front office.

That divide could become an important part of the offseason conversation. Still, it would be premature to conclude that Mitchell is leaving because of Clark .

The two have developed into one of the WNBA's most productive scoring combinations, and their partnership has been a major reason for Indiana's improvement.

The Fever also have a clear incentive to retain an elite veteran who can shoot at a high level while taking some of the offensive burden away from Clark . Mitchell , meanwhile, has earned the right to examine every option.

After nine seasons with one franchise, a career-best statistical year and a growing role alongside one of the sport's biggest stars, her decision will likely come down to what environment she believes best fits the next stage of her career.

For the Fever , keeping Mitchell would preserve the core of a team that believes it can eventually compete for a championship. For Mitchell , however, her latest comments make clear that basketball will not be the only consideration.

articles.title: Sheryl Swoopes takes another jab at Caitlin Clark: “One player showed up, the other didn’t”
articles.standfirst: WNBA legend insists the series was never simply Clark versus Wilson
articles.summary: WNBA legend insists the series was never simply Clark versus Wilson
articles.body:
Sheryl Swoopes has reignited the debate around Caitlin Clark and A’ja Wilson after the Indiana Fever ’s playoff elimination, making clear she believes Wilson was the player who truly seized the moment.

The WNBA Hall of Famer stopped short of reducing the series to a one-on-one rivalry, but her assessment left little room for ambiguity.

Speaking on the Levels To This Podcast, Swoopes revisited the criticism Wilson had faced before the postseason, including comments suggesting the Las Vegas Aces star was uncomfortable sharing the spotlight with Clark.

Swoopes had already dismissed that line of thinking, and she argued Wilson didn't need any outside motivation once the playoffs began.

“If you’re a player like A’ja Wilson, you really don’t need any motivation,” Swoopes said. “Your motivation is: I am that girl. Like, I am her. I am the four-time, soon-to-be five-time MVP. So I’m just going to go do what I do.”

She then delivered the line that has drawn the most attention. “I’m not saying that this game was A’ja versus Caitlin. Right. It was Aces versus Fever . Yep. But one player showed up, and the other player didn’t.”

Wilson answered with dominant playoff performances

The numbers supported Swoopes ’ argument about Wilson ’s impact. The four-time MVP opened the series with 38 points, 16 rebounds and four blocks as Las Vegas beat Indiana 102-85, setting the tone with a performance the Fever never truly solved.

Indiana responded in Game 2 with a 99-89 victory to force a decider, but Wilson still scored 22 points. The series then swung decisively back toward Las Vegas in Game 3, when she produced 36 points and 10 rebounds in a 94-83 win that sent the Aces through.

Swoopes’ co-host Terrika Foster-Brasby was equally emphatic. “A’ja Wilson is absolutely that… girl,” she said. “In game one, literally, there was nothing that could be done with her. Indiana threw multiple defenders at her. She ate them all up.”

Clark finished the deciding game with 18 points and six turnovers, while Kelsey Mitchell scored 23 and Aliyah Boston added 19. Indiana had enough offensive production to remain competitive, but Wilson’s efficiency and physical presence proved too much over the course of the series.

Swoopes’ point was about the moment

The significance of Swoopes ’ comments lies less in diminishing Clark and more in how she framed Wilson’s response to the pressure surrounding the matchup.

She repeatedly stressed that this was an Aces-Fever series, not a personal duel, while still arguing that one superstar rose more decisively to the occasion.

That matters because the Clark-Wilson conversation has often been pulled into broader debates around media attention, popularity and status within the league.

Swoopes ’ position is that when the postseason demanded a defining performance, Wilson delivered it. Las Vegas now advances to face the Golden State Valkyries , with Wilson again at the center of another championship run.

If she maintains the level she showed against Indiana, Swoopes may not be the only one arguing that the gap between Wilson and the rest of the league remains significant.

articles.title: Janelle Salaün makes history in the WNBA and wins an award unanimously
articles.standfirst: French Golden State player Janelle Salaün already has her first major individual award in the WNBA. The Golden State Valkyries' French player was unanimously chosen as the 2026 Sixth Player of the Year after receiving all 74 votes from the national panel responsible for deciding the award.
articles.summary: French Golden State player Janelle Salaün already has her first major individual award in the WNBA. The Golden State Valkyries' French player was unanimously chosen as the 2026 Sixth Player of the Year after receiving all 74 votes from the national panel responsible for deciding the award.
articles.body:
"J anelle Salaün already has her first major individual award in the WNBA. The French player for the Golden State Valkyries was chosen 2026 Sixth Woman of the Year by unanimous vote, after receiving all 74 votes from the national panel responsible for deciding the award.

Her season explains the difference. Salaün finished as the leading scorer among bench players, with 12.7 points per game, and set a new WNBA record for a reserve with 509 points in a single season.

A record-breaking season for Salaün

The French player appeared in the 40 games of the regular season and came off the bench in all of them. In 22.1 minutes per game, she averaged 12.7 points, 4.0 rebounds and 1.2 assists , shooting 42.5% from the field and 39.2% from three-point range.

Her production left more historical marks. Salaün finished the season with the records for a reserve i n total points (509), three-pointers made (93), and games with at least 10 points (27).

She also reached 20 points on six occasions , a figure that leaves her tied for fourth place all-time by a reserve in a single season.

From rookie to leader of the second unit

Salaün's leap came just one year after her arrival in the WNBA. The Frenchwoman was named to the 2025 All-Rookie Team, and in her second season she became one of the main offensive references of Golden State's second unit.

Her production helped the Valkyries complete a 32-12 regular season, the second-best record in the WNBA. The team also improved notably from its first year in the league, when it finished with 23 wins.

Salaün was chosen ahead of Sophie Cunningham, Cameron Brink, and Jewell Loyd, but ultimately prevailed with the unanimous backing of the panel.

The award comes before the semifinals

The individual recognition also comes in the midst of Golden State's title run. The Valkyries began their semifinal series against the Las Vegas Aces this Sunday after defeating the Dallas Wings in the first round.

Salaün faces that playoff series after completing a season in which she left her name in several WNBA record books. The Sixth Woman of the Year award is the individual recognition for a campaign that had already been marked by her records off the bench.

articles.title: Angel Reese stole the spotlight before Dream-Liberty with this look
articles.standfirst: Fashion took over the WNBA semifinals.
articles.summary: Fashion took over the WNBA semifinals.
articles.body:
The Atlanta Dream arrived at State Farm Arena in Atlanta , Georgia, this Sunday, October 4, to face the New York Liberty in Game 1 of the WNBA semifinals.

Among the players arriving for such an important matchup was Angel Reese , who had already drawn plenty of attention before stepping onto the court.

What outfit did she wear?

For this game, Reese left any sportswear references behind and opted for a long-sleeve black romper with a V-neckline , featuring a fitted and structured silhouette.

The look continued with black knee-high heeled boots, while the contrast came from her handbag, an animal-print design in shades of yellow, gold and black.

Angel added gold jewelry, including several bracelets and long earrings, while wearing her black hair loose, voluminous and styled in soft waves .

But the pregame look was left behind once it was time to play.

Atlanta and New York entered the matchup with the same goal: winning the opening game of a best-of-five series . The difference came after halftime, when the Dream found the stretch that completely changed the direction of the game.

The third quarter was the turning point. Atlanta scored 32 points and held the Liberty to 15 , giving the Dream enough separation heading into the final period to keep New York at a distance.

Jordin Canada led Atlanta in scoring with 25 points, while the Dream closed out the game with a 92-82 victory .

What did Angel Reese contribute?

Reese finished her first semifinal game with 17 points, seven rebounds, four steals and three blocks in 34 minutes .

She also went 6-for-10 from the field and made an impact on both ends of the court. Her four steals and three blocks were part of a strong defensive performance that helped Atlanta contain New York during the decisive stretches.

Atlanta is already looking ahead to Game 2

The Dream and Liberty will meet again on Wednesday, October 7 , at State Farm Arena, where Atlanta will look to take a 2-0 series lead before the matchup shifts elsewhere.

New York, meanwhile, will need to respond in Game 2 to avoid falling even further behind.

articles.title: The Caitlin Clark effect is taking a toll on her Indiana Fever teammates: “We're being criticized for being on her team”
articles.standfirst: Aliyah Boston and Kelsey Mitchell have described the intense scrutiny surrounding the Fever, while Amber Cox continues to defend Indiana's supporters
articles.summary: Aliyah Boston and Kelsey Mitchell have described the intense scrutiny surrounding the Fever, while Amber Cox continues to defend Indiana's supporters
articles.body:
C aitlin Clark has transformed the Indiana Fever into one of the WNBA's biggest attractions, but the attention surrounding the superstar has also created an uncomfortable reality for some of her teammates.

That tension has become increasingly visible following Indiana's first-round playoff exit against the Las Vegas Aces , with Aliyah Boston and Kelsey Mitchell both discussing the treatment they have received from portions of the Fever fan base.

Their comments came shortly after Fever general manager Amber Cox strongly defended Indiana supporters against criticism over their behavior.

The disagreement has created an unusual divide between the organization's leadership and players who say the experience of playing for the Fever can sometimes be difficult.

Boston described having to deal with harsh comments earlier in the season before seeing the tone change once Indiana began winning more games.

“Being on this team to start this season, I was at the other end of those hate comments,” Boston said after Indiana’s season ended in a playoff series loss to Las Vegas.

“I was at the end of every single thing that succumbed. They say they support the Fever and everything like that, but… they just said everything under the earth. That was a big reason why I took a break from social media.”

The former No. 1 overall pick also pointed to what she saw as a dramatic shift in how supporters treated her when the team's fortunes improved.

“At the same time it’s like now that the tables have turned and we started winning games, and we had something better in their opinion, then all of a sudden it was like love comments, ‘oh my gosh, you’re doing amazing.’”

Mitchell , meanwhile, focused specifically on what comes with playing alongside Clark . The veteran guard has spent her entire WNBA career with Indiana and produced the best scoring season of her career in 2026, averaging 24.7 points per game.

“Showing up every day to compete for fans that may or may not like you is hard,” she said. “Playing with (Caitlin Clark) and having the eyes that she got, we get a lot of flak for just being on her team.”

The Fever's popularity has brought unprecedented attention

There is little question that Clark's arrival has dramatically changed the scale of attention surrounding Indiana.

The Fever went 28-16 during the 2026 regular season, with Clark averaging 22.3 points and 8.3 assists per game while Mitchell averaged 24.7 points and Boston added 16.1 points and 8.0 rebounds.

But increased visibility can also magnify everything that happens around the team. Praise, criticism, social-media arguments and individual performances all receive considerably more attention when Clark is involved.

That was evident during the season when Boston and Mitchell publicly backed head coach Stephanie White after fans booed her introduction at a home game.

Clark also said she understood that fans could disagree with decisions but made clear that the team would support its coach.

The issue resurfaced in the playoffs. During Indiana's series against Las Vega s, Aces star A'ja Wilson confronted a Fever fan after he pointed at her during Game 2.

The Fever later clarified that the spectator had not violated the team's Fan Code of Conduct and was not removed from the arena.

That incident became part of the larger conversation about the environment around Indiana games, although it is important not to characterize every Fever supporter in the same way.

Former Fever forward Brianna Turner , who now plays for Las Vegas, nevertheless pushed back strongly against Cox's defense of the fan base.

“This is an unequivocally false statement,” Turner said. “Players inside and outside the organization have repeatedly issued complaints with the Fever fan base. While it’s not all Indy fans, it’s certainly a trend. To say the attacks have ‘no basis in reality’ is disingenuous.”

Cox has maintained that the overwhelming majority of Indiana supporters have behaved appropriately and that criticism of the entire fan base is unfair.

“The attacks on our fanbase have no basis in reality, and they need to stop,” Cox said.

“Especially with members of the media. … I’m talking about media who have never been to a game at Gainbridge Fieldhouse. Every organization in the league, every organization throughout professional sports, all the way down to youth rec leagues, have to deal with occasional bad behavior from spectators. And anyone who crosses the line in an arena or online needs to be held accountable. I want to be really clear about that. There is a line, and people need to be held accountable if they cross it.

“But here’s the fact: We did not have one fan pointed out by a player who violated the WNBA code of conduct this season. Not one fan was removed from a game. … Our fans love this team. They’re going to cheer, they’re going to boo, and sometimes they might point. It’s a home-court advantage for a reason, and it’s the same for the Pacers. And all of that is within the code of conduct.”

The disagreement does not necessarily mean Clark herself is the source of tension inside the Fever .

In fact, Mitchell's comments suggest something more complicated: the extraordinary level of attention surrounding Clark can spill over onto everyone associated with her.

For Boston, who was already a centerpiece of the Fever before Clark arrived, that attention has meant dealing with criticism and then a sudden reversal when her performances improved.

For Mitchell , it has meant becoming part of a global spotlight that did not exist at the same level during the earlier stages of her career. That is the double-edged nature of the Caitlin Clark effect.

Her presence has helped make the Fever one of the WNBA's most watched teams and has created enormous exposure for the players around her.

But that exposure also means teammates can find themselves pulled into online debates and criticism simply because they wear the same uniform.

Indiana now enters an important offseason after another first-round playoff defeat. Keeping Clark, Mitchell and Boston together remains a major priority for the franchise, but the organization will also have to consider how it handles the enormous expectations surrounding its players.

The Fever's popularity is unlikely to disappear. If anything, it is likely to grow.

The challenge will be making sure the attention that has helped transform the franchise into one of the WNBA's biggest draws does not become an unnecessary burden for the players expected to turn that popularity into postseason success.

articles.title: Sophie Cunningham: “I found my superpower when I stopped trying to be like everyone else”
articles.standfirst: The Indiana Fever player recalled how her height and athletic build made her different during her childhood.
articles.summary: The Indiana Fever player recalled how her height and athletic build made her different during her childhood.
articles.body:
Sophie Cunningham didn’t always feel comfortable with what is now part of her identity. The Indiana Fever player recalled that during her childhood she was taller and more strongly built than many girls her age and that she even was teased for being bigger than some boys .

She shared it during her appearance on Sons & Daughters, the podcast hosted by Shannon Spake . Cunningham explained that she grew up surrounded by tall, athletic women: her mother is 1.78 meters tall, her aunt is 1.91, and her grandmother is also 1.78. She and her sister Lindsey even wished they would reach 1.83 meters.

'From mockery to "superpower"'

Cunningham herself recalled how she experienced that difference when she was a child. Her family managed to turn what was then a cause for jokes into one of her greatest strengths.

“They made fun of me for being bigger, for being taller than the boys, for looking different from the other girls and for not being small, for having a more athletic build”, she explained.

But at home she received a very different message. Her mother, her aunt, and her grandmother did not want her to try to hide what made her different. On the contrary, they kept telling her that one day that difference would be precisely one of her greatest advantages.

“That is going to be your greatest superpower someday. Pull your shoulders back”, Cunningham recalled about one of the pieces of advice she received from her family.

Over the years, that difference ended up becoming a tool. Cunningham played several sports during her childhood and adolescence, including basketball, volleyball, track and field, and American football. In college, she especially stood out in basketball and ended up becoming one of the great players of Rock Bridge High School before arriving at the University of Missouri.

“I found my superpower when I stopped trying to be like everyone else”

The idea resurfaced when Cunningham spoke about her college years. The player explained that for a long time she had tried to fit in, until she understood that her greatest advantage lay precisely in stopping.

“I think I really found my superpower when I stopped trying to be like everyone else. I simply was myself”, she said as she recalled her decision to play at Missouri.

There she ended up becoming the all-time leading scorer in the Tigers women's program, with 2,187 points, before making the jump to the WNBA .

His intention, she explained, was always to combine that strength with her feminine side. “Yes, I’m tall and maybe I’m not small, but I’m still strong. I want to wear heels. I want to be feminine. I want to be a badass on the court”, she said.

A lesson that stayed with her all the way to the WNBA

What once made her feel different during her childhood ended up becoming part of the player she is today.

Cunningham has built much of her public persona around self-confidence and not worrying too much about what others think , something that also appears as one of the main themes of her conversation with Shannon Spake.

The height, physique, and personality that were once the subject of jokes ended up becoming part of her strengths . Her family had warned her when she was still a child: one day, the very thing that made her different could become her greatest advantage.

articles.title: Indiana Fever faces challenge of keeping Caitlin Clark happy so she doesn't consider leaving
articles.standfirst: With Clark, Cunningham and Mitchell central to the conversation, Indiana’s next roster moves could shape its championship window
articles.summary: With Clark, Cunningham and Mitchell central to the conversation, Indiana’s next roster moves could shape its championship window
articles.body:
The Indiana Fever entered the playoffs as the No.6 seed with hopes of making a deeper run, but the defending WNBA champion Las Vegas Aces ended those plans in three games.

Las Vegas closed the series with a 94-83 win in Game 3, holding Caitlin Clark to 18 points on 6-of-18 shooting. She added four assists, two steals and four blocks, but Indiana could not do enough to extend its season.

That defeat has shifted attention toward an offseason filled with contract questions and roster decisions.

Linda Cohn believes the Fever ’s biggest task is clear: improving the team around Clark rather than simply rewarding its core players financially.

“That doesn’t mean she should take less money,” Cohn said on The Linda Cohn Show. “It means Indiana has to do more than pay its stars. It still has to improve the roster around them.”

Clark’s future matters, but so does the roster

Clark remains under contract through 2027 after Indiana exercised its team option, but she is already eligible to negotiate an EPIC extension after earning All-WNBA honors within the first three years of her rookie deal.

Cohn said the structure of that eventual agreement could become one of the most important questions facing the franchise.

“Will Clark have an out if expectations are not met?” she asked. “Whether Clark does something similar, this is going to be an interesting basketball question.”

Clark ’s value to Indiana is obvious. She averaged 22.3 points, 4.0 rebounds and 8.3 assists this season and remained one of the league’s biggest television draws.

Indiana also had all 44 regular-season games carried on national networks. But Cohn argued the Fever still need more around her defensively.

“Give Clark another perimeter defender,” she said. “Give Boston more frontcourt help.”

Multiple major decisions beyond Clark

The offseason won't revolve around Clark alone. Sophie Cunningham is an unrestricted free agent after returning on a one-year deal, while Kelsey Mitchell , Indiana’s leading scorer this season, is also headed toward free agency.

Cohn highlighted Cunningham ’s influence beyond traditional statistics.

“Amber Cox clearly values what she brings beyond the box score,” Cohn said. “Cox called Sophie a leader, a connector, and an important voice in the locker room. Well, that matters.”

She also pointed to head coach Stephanie White ’s emphasis on establishing a more consistent defensive identity.

White referenced the standard once set by Tamika Catchings , and Cohn said Indiana needs to find players capable of bringing that same edge.

The Fever already have their centerpiece in Clark and another foundational piece in Aaliyah Boston .

The next step is building a roster that gives them enough defensive resistance, depth and lineup flexibility to avoid another early postseason exit.

That may be the most important decision Indiana makes this offseason.

articles.title: Sophie Cunningham found a new rival after being eliminated from the playoffs
articles.standfirst: Who is it?
articles.summary: Who is it?
articles.body:
The Indiana Fever’s season came to an end last Thursday, October 1, with a 94-83 loss to the Las Vegas Aces in the WNBA playoffs . For Sophie Cunningham, it was time to put away her game shoes, although she still had one last matchup left.

Only this time, there was no WNBA court involved . Cunningham traded the hardwood for the mini hoop at home and found a rival she knew much better: her dad.

Sophie set him a challenge

The player shared the moment on her Instagram Stories when she decided to put him to the test. The challenge seemed simple, but Sophie wanted to add an incentive that would make every shot count.

The bet was clear: if her dad made the basket, he could eat chips and fast food for a week .

Before he took the shot, Cunningham warned him to be careful with the fan. He gave it a try, but his first attempt missed .

Sophie gave him a second chance, and the two decided to raise the stakes with double or nothing. This time, making the basket would mean two weeks of chips and fast food .

There was no miss this time. The ball went through the hoop , and Sophie reacted with surprise, as if she did not expect her dad to actually make it. But the basket counted, and so did the bet.

Beyond this fun and sweet moment at home, Sophie Cunningham is already beginning to look ahead. Her contract with Indiana is for one year and $600,000, meaning that with the 2026 season coming to an end, she will become a free agent heading into 2027 .

That will once again leave her with a decision to make about her future: remain with the Fever or explore the possibility of wearing another WNBA team’s jersey.

articles.title: Warning for Caitlin Clark: "If Kelsey Mitchell leaves, the Indiana Fever are done"
articles.standfirst: Indiana’s offseason could hinge on whether its four-time All-Star chooses to stay or explore a new opportunity
articles.summary: Indiana’s offseason could hinge on whether its four-time All-Star chooses to stay or explore a new opportunity
articles.body:
Cheryl Miller has delivered a blunt warning to the Indiana Fever as Kelsey Mitchell approaches unrestricted free agency: losing the four-time All-Star could dramatically alter the franchise’s direction.

Speaking on WNBA Showtime, Miller urged Indiana to keep Mitchell happy and retain her, arguing that the Fever’s outlook could change completely if their veteran guard walks away.

“You better make that young lady happy,” Miller said. “You better keep Kelsey Mitchell there. Otherwise, Indiana Fever, it’s a wrap. It’s a wrap for you if that young lady leaves.”

The timing makes the warning significant. Indiana has just been eliminated by the Las Vegas Aces, while Mitchell is preparing to enter an open market for the first time in her career.

Mitchell’s leverage comes after a remarkable 2026 campaign. She averaged 24.7 points per game and finished with 1,086 points, a new single-season WNBA record. She also produced 27 consecutive games with at least 20 points, another league record.

Those numbers explain why Indiana views keeping her as a major offseason priority. General manager Amber Cox has made it clear that the organization wants Mitchell to remain a Fever player for the rest of her career.

“She has a lot of equity in this franchise and has put in a lot of time,” said Cox . “Kelsey obviously has the opportunity and has earned the right to explore what other opportunities are out there, but our goal is for her to be a Fever girl for the rest of her career.”

Mitchell’s decision could reshape Indiana’s plans

The complication is that Mitchell has made it clear that loyalty won’t be the only factor in her decision. After the playoff exit, she said she needs to be “selfish” about what’s best for her career, including winning and individual success.

She also discussed the unusual pressures that come with playing for the Fever alongside Caitlin Clark.

That leaves Indiana with an important balancing act. Aliyah Boston has already signed a major contract extension, while Clark is also expected to receive a significant long-term deal. With more money committed to its young stars, the Fever could face difficult decisions when trying to retain Mitchell .

Still, losing Mitchell wouldn’t necessarily end Indiana’s competitive ambitions. Her departure would free significant salary-cap space, giving the front office an opportunity to reshape the roster rather than simply finding another player to replicate everything Mitchell provides.

Her scoring, shot-making and ability to create offense would be difficult to replace, but Indiana could use the available money to address several weaknesses at once.

The Fever could prioritize defensive versatility, athletic wings, frontcourt depth and perimeter shooting around Clark and Boston . Building a more balanced roster could help Indiana avoid becoming overly dependent on its offensive firepower, particularly against elite teams capable of exploiting defensive mismatches.

Players such as Dallas Wings forward Awak Kuier or Los Angeles Sparks wing Rae Burrell have been mentioned as examples of the type of talent Indiana could pursue. Kelsey Plum could also be an option on the market, although the Fever might prefer to spread Mitchell’s salary slot across multiple additions.

articles.title: Caitlin Clark says goodbye to a Fever teammate as Indiana clears space for her new contract
articles.standfirst: For the second consecutive season, the Fever were eliminated by the Las Vegas Aces and MVP A'ja Wilson
articles.summary: For the second consecutive season, the Fever were eliminated by the Las Vegas Aces and MVP A'ja Wilson
articles.body:
The season for the Indiana Fever concluded in a familiar fashion, suffering an early exit at the hands of the Las Vegas Aces in the first round of the playoffs, a postseason format that should be expanded from a best-of-three to a grueling best-of-five series.

After missing 31 of the team’s 44 regular-season games in 2025 alongside the entirety of the playoff run due to a lingering injury, superstar guard Caitlin Clark mounted a triumphant return in 2026 , shattering both individual and league milestones.

Clark delivered a sensational MVP-caliber campaign , finishing third in the league in points per game (22.3) and second in assists (8.3) while becoming the first player in WNBA history to rank inside the top three in both major statistical categories, complemented by an unprecedented 41.2 points created per game .

With the chapter closed on a brilliant individual year, the Fever front office faces an urgent offseason agenda, headlined by the priority to re-sign Kelsey Mitchell , who also posted an MVP-level season, while filling out a roster that currently features only six players under contract , with veteran Sophie Cunningham widely anticipated to look for opportunities elsewhere.

Caitlin Clark Farewell to Harris as Indiana Prepares for Roster Overhaul

Amidst the offseason roster restructuring, veteran guard Tyasha Harris, whose year was cut short after suffering a broken fibula in the team's regular-season finale, shared a retrospective carousel of photos capturing cherished moments with her Fever teammates.

Expressing deep gratitude for the opportunity to represent her hometown franchise, Harris drew an outpouring of online support , highlighted by a brief yet affectionate farewell from Indiana's cornerstone: "Love you homie," commented the league's most popular player.

Across 39 appearances this season, Harris provided steady minutes off the bench, averaging 4 points and 13 minutes per contest.

While a potential return to Indiana remains mathematically possible, any new contract hinges heavily on the franchise's broader financial flexibility, particularly the impending max extension for Clark and the necessity of locking up Mitchell to preserve their core trio alongside Aliyah Boston .

Should the front office successfully execute these moves, Cunningham will almost certainly depart in free agency, allowing the eight-year veteran to secure a prominent role with a new club as the Fever double down on their championship foundation.

articles.title: Caitlin Clark is gearing up for another historic new sneaker launch, and Nike is rubbing its hands in anticipation
articles.standfirst: The Fever star’s latest colorway turns a historic rookie-season milestone into a bold new release
articles.summary: The Fever star’s latest colorway turns a historic rookie-season milestone into a bold new release
articles.body:
Caitlin Clark’s first signature sneaker with Nike has barely reached stores, yet the next chapter is already waiting in the wings. The Caitlin 1 made its global retail debut on October 1, giving fans the first chance to buy the shoe built around the Indiana Fever guard’s explosive style and long-range shooting.

Now Nike is preparing to keep that momentum rolling with the Caitlin 1 “Midnight Fever.” Scheduled for October 14, the new colorway brings a Hot Punch and Neo Pink palette to Clark’s debut signature model.

Its Opticast upper fades with vibrant pink tones, giving the sneaker one of its most eye-catching appearances yet.

The release also has a personal connection to one of Clark’s most memorable achievements during her rookie season. The colorway celebrates her 22nd game in the WNBA, when she became the first rookie in league history to record a triple-double.

Clark finished that July 6, 2024, matchup against the New York Liberty with 19 points, 12 rebounds and 13 assists, while also becoming the first player in Fever history to post a triple-double.

The number 22 has an obvious connection to Clark , who wears the same number, making the inspiration behind the sneaker particularly fitting as it turns a significant statistical milestone from her first professional season into a design detail that fans can carry onto the court.

A signature launch with serious momentum

The attention surrounding the “Midnight Fever” is understandable after the Caitlin 1’s opening reception. Nike describes the model as its first signature shoe for Clark , combining an Air Zoom Turbo unit, Cushlon foam and a lightweight Opticast upper to support quick movement and responsiveness.

Clark was also closely involved in the design process, with personal touches including her CC logo, multiple references to 22 and double Swooshes.

Nike has positioned the launch as a major moment for its women’s basketball business, too. Company executives have described the Caitlin 1 as the largest women’s signature shoe launch in Nike’s history, with the initial rollout reaching 5,000 retail doors worldwide.

That distribution is roughly twice the average footprint for a Nike signature basketball shoe, highlighting the level of confidence surrounding Clark’s brand.

The timing is notable as Nike continues expanding its women’s basketball roster. Clark now sits alongside fellow WNBA stars A’ja Wilson and Sabrina Ionescu , giving the company several prominent signature athletes as interest in the women’s game continues to grow.

After the attention surrounding the original Caitlin 1 launch, another strong demand surge would hardly be surprising. Nike has already shown it believes Clark can move the needle, and this vibrant follow-up gives the company another opportunity to turn her on-court impact into one of basketball’s most talked-about stories.

articles.title: Caitlin Clark exposes the WNBA without even playing: The stat that doesn't sit well with Angel Reese or A'ja Wilson
articles.standfirst: One playoff crowd has reignited the debate over Clark’s unprecedented WNBA impact
articles.summary: One playoff crowd has reignited the debate over Clark’s unprecedented WNBA impact
articles.body:
Caitlin Clark’s influence on the WNBA is being debated again, but the latest attendance numbers have made the argument harder to ignore.

Even with Clark sitting at home, her impact remains visible whenever teams compare crowds before and after her arrival.

That was especially apparent in Atlanta. The Dream welcomed 17,044 fans to State Farm Arena when the Indiana Fever came to town, while previous Clark appearances at the building had also produced enormous crowds.

Atlanta increasingly moved games into the much larger arena to accommodate demand, giving Clark’s visits an unmistakable box-office effect. Then came the playoffs.

When Atlanta hosted the New York Liberty in Game 1 of the semifinals, announced attendance was 9,745. The upper level was largely closed, creating an immediate visual contrast with the packed crowds seen when Clark and Indiana visited.

Former NBA player Etan Thomas highlighted the crowd while arguing that the WNBA could thrive without Clark , but the post quickly attracted criticism after fans pointed to the actual attendance figure.

The comparison was particularly striking because Atlanta had already demonstrated what can happen when Clark arrives. In 2008, the franchise had established an attendance record of 11,609 at Philips Arena, now State Farm Arena.

That mark survived for 16 years. Clark helped change the equation, with Indiana games producing crowds well above the old record.

The numbers tell a more complicated story

The situation, however, isn't as simple as claiming Atlanta couldn't sell tickets without Clark . The Dream explained that their playoff schedule was finalized only days before the opening game, leaving the organization with limited time to market and sell tickets.

The team initially opened only the lower bowl, which holds around 8,800 fans, before eventually releasing additional upper-level seats.

That explanation matters because Atlanta's overall attendance picture has improved substantially. The Dream averaged 6,928 fans during the regular season, nearly 2,500 more per game than the previous year. Their increased use of State Farm Arena was a major factor, with six regular-season games played there in 2026.

Still, Clark’s drawing power is difficult to dismiss. Atlanta's biggest crowds repeatedly came when Indiana was involved, demonstrating how strongly Clark can influence demand in opposing markets.

The Fever have experienced a similar phenomenon across the league, with road games attracting unusually large audiences and, in some cases, forcing teams to relocate matchups to larger venues.

Clark's influence also extends beyond attendance. After Indiana's playoff elimination, she returned to Iowa City for ESPN's College GameDay, serving as a guest picker and reconnecting with the community that helped establish her as a basketball superstar. She missed the Fever's exit interviews because of that previously scheduled commitment.

So the fairest conclusion isn't that Clark single-handedly carries the WNBA. The league has major stars such as Angel Reese and A'ja Wilson, while franchises like Atlanta are clearly building their own audiences.

articles.title: Angel Reese receives an electric standing ovation while tasting a real shot at a title
articles.standfirst: The Atlanta crowd is giving Reese a taste of what she has been chasing all season
articles.summary: The Atlanta crowd is giving Reese a taste of what she has been chasing all season
articles.body:
A ngel Reese could become the first of the new generation of WNBA stars to reach the Finals and have a real chance at winning a championship . Her decision to transfer to Atlanta and find the momentum she needed to make the playoffs was heavily questioned at first.

But the city has made Reese feel welcomed and supported. The results and numbers are there to back up a move that initially did not convince some fans, who believed changing teams would not give her the stability she needed to compete for a title. Reese could now be close to proving that theory wrong.

Atlanta is showing Reese just how much the city is behind her

The popularity of the WNBA's new generation has grown exponentially, but Reese's rise has also come with a wave of criticism compared with the support Caitlin Clark and Paige Bueckers have received . Now, Reese is getting a different kind of response as Atlanta continues to rally around her.

Reese could be the first from this group of young stars to truly compete for a WNBA championship after already becoming the first new superstar to claim an end-of-season award. Caitlin Clark, Paige Bueckers, Olivia Miles, Sonia Citron and Kiki Iriafen were all eliminated in the first round of the playoffs this year.

Reese is embracing the moment as Atlanta dreams of the Finals

That leaves Reese as the first young superstar to play in the semifinals . The Fever reached this stage last year, but Clark was injured, leaving Reese as the only one from this group still standing alongside the veteran stars competing for this year's championship.

Reese is savoring the moment because she is finally experiencing what she wanted so badly. The support from the fans, the towels being waved for her and the way Atlanta has backed her are delivering the kind of support she was looking for. The Dream have a realistic shot at the Finals.

articles.standfirst: Angel Reese has shown this season that starting over somewhere else does not mean starting from scratch, even when the spotlight is on other stars.
articles.summary: Angel Reese has shown this season that starting over somewhere else does not mean starting from scratch, even when the spotlight is on other stars.
articles.body:
In 2026, Reese had to adjust to a new team, a new locker room and a new dynamic with the Atlanta Dream . Her place as a star was already established, but now she had to prove she could maintain that level in a completely different environment from the one she had known during her first years in the WNBA .

articles.summary: Midnight Fever arrives next, while Halloween, Chiefs-inspired and Friendship Bracelet editions give fans more reasons to watch the release calendar
articles.body:
Caitlin Clark’s first signature Nike shoe made a fast impression. The Caitlin Blue and Warning Code editions launched on October 1 and quickly sold out in almost every size online, according to Sports Illustrated. For fans who missed that first opportunity, the next releases offer another chance to buy a pair at retail.

The next date to circle is October 14, 2026 , when Hibbett will release the pink Midnight Fever edition. Nike lists the shoe at $140 in adult sizes , while Hibbett has published the launch date on its own website. Beyond that release, the calendar stretches into February 2027, although several dates remain reported schedules rather than announcements verified directly with Nike.

Nike Caitlin 1 release dates: What is coming next?

The following calendar reflects retailer announcements and current sneaker-media reporting. Availability can vary by market, and future dates remain subject to change.

Fans have more chances to find their favorite Caitlin 1 . Midnight Fever launches October 14, followed by an expected Halloween release on October 23. Cave Stone is scheduled for November 3, while December brings Ice Cold on the 1st, Purple Venom on the 12th and Sea of Red on the 21st.

Looking ahead to 2027, Triple Black is expected January 5, followed by Friendship Bracelet on February 24. Apart from Hibbett’s confirmed Midnight Fever launch, these dates reflect sneaker-media reporting and remain subject to change.

The October-to-December schedule is supported by Sports Illustrated, Nice Kicks and other specialist publications. SneakerFiles lists the January release, while Hypebeast reports an expected February launch for Friendship Bracelet.

There is more to the collection than changing colors. Midnight Fever references Clark’s first WNBA triple-double, while Purple Venom draws inspiration from the ultraviolet vision of hawks a connection to her Iowa roots and the way she sees opportunities on the court. Cave Stone takes a quieter approach, with sandy tones intended to reflect composure under pressure.

Underneath those designs, the Caitlin 1 remains a performance basketball shoe. Nike describes a lightweight Opticast upper , forefoot Air Zoom Turbo cushioning and Cushlon foam . Clark’s initials and number appear throughout the design, while cement-inspired textures recall the driveway court where she developed her game. Those details turn the collection into a small record of the player’s journey.

For shoppers, the immediate opportunity is Midnight Fever on October 14. Fans waiting for a later edition should check Nike’s U.S. listings and participating retailers as their preferred date approaches.

articles.title: Caitlin Clark and Kelsey Mitchell bring Indiana Fever's locker room closer together just before possible farewell
articles.standfirst: Indiana stars showed support for Aliyah Boston as Mitchell prepares for a potentially defining free-agency decision
articles.summary: Indiana stars showed support for Aliyah Boston as Mitchell prepares for a potentially defining free-agency decision
articles.body:
The Indiana Fever walked away from their WNBA first-round loss to the Las Vegas Aces with plenty to think about, but one thing appears settled, which is the connection inside the locker room is still strong.

Indiana pushed the series to three games before falling 94-83 in the deciding matchup. A’ja Wilson finished with 36 points and 10 rebounds, while Chelsea Gray added 23 points, four rebounds and five assists.

Kelsey Mitchell led the Fever with 23 points. Aliyah Boston had 19 points and 10 rebounds, while Caitlin Clark added 18 points, four assists, two steals and four blocks.

A few days later, Boston offered a glimpse of how the team was processing the end of the season. “Year 4 [check],” she wrote on social media. “In all things I give thanks!”

Clark responded with a short message of support. “Proud of u!” she wrote. Mitchell followed with one of her own: “love you, 7.”

Mitchell’s free agency gives messages added weight

Those comments would normally be easy to overlook, but the timing makes them more significant.

Mitchell is set to enter unrestricted free agency and has already made it clear that she intends to prioritize what is best for her career when deciding what comes next.

She also said that having “good chemistry on and off the floor” will be part of that process. That matters because Mitchell has grown with this Fever group.

She and Boston have been teammates since Boston arrived as the No.1 overall pick in the 2023 WNBA Draft, and they have experienced Indiana’s transformation together.

The franchise went from missing the playoffs to carrying legitimate postseason expectations. Clark ’s arrival only accelerated that rise.

Fever face difficult offseason question

The next challenge is deciding how much of that core remains together. Indiana has obvious reasons to build around Clark and Boston , but Mitchell ’s situation introduces uncertainty.

She has established herself as one of the team’s most important scorers, and losing her would force the Fever to rethink the balance of their backcourt. There's also a human side to that decision.

Mitchell ’s message to Boston , along with Clark ’s response, showed that this group remains close despite the disappointment of an early playoff exit. That doesn't guarantee Mitchell will return.

It does, however, make clear that any potential departure wouldn't come because the locker room has fractured. Indiana ’s season ended with frustration against Las Vegas , but the players themselves have spent the days since emphasizing appreciation rather than disappointment.

As the Fever head into an offseason that could reshape the roster, that bond may become one of the biggest factors in determining whether this group gets another chance together.

articles.title: Sophie Cunningham sends another message to the WNBA, sparking yet more controversy
articles.standfirst: The Fever guard made another pointed statement months after her comments on transgender participation sparked national debate
articles.summary: The Fever guard made another pointed statement months after her comments on transgender participation sparked national debate
articles.body:
Sophie Cunningham has spent much of the past year becoming one of the most outspoken players in the WNBA , and her latest appearance ensured that the conversation around her would continue well beyond basketball.

The Indiana Fever guard returned to Missouri for the school’s homecoming football game wearing a hat that read “No Cis Just … Woman,” with “Woman” displayed prominently across the front. When Cunningham was introduced on the field, she pointed toward the message with both hands.

The gesture immediately drew attention because it closely followed comments she had already made about transgender participation in women’s sports.

“I got a lot of negative feedback about me hating trans. And I’m like, ‘I never once said that,’” Cunningham previously told ESPN. “I think that I am here to extend love.

"But I also think with that love is truth, being honest. And I want to protect young girls in a locker room, or young girls in sport who shouldn’t have to go against biological men.”

Cunningham shows no sign of backing away

Those comments had already generated strong reactions from supporters and critics alike. Cunningham later reinforced her position while speaking with reporters, saying she believed the issue came down to protecting girls in competition.

“I think it’s really important to protect children, and that’s little girls who are also involved in that category,” she said. “And so I’ll stand on what I said, and I’ll always believe that.”

Her remarks became a recurring talking point around Fever games, with demonstrators from opposing sides of the debate appearing outside arenas and Cunningham facing boos from some opposing crowds.

She also posed for photographs later in the season with Jennifer Sey and Riley Gaines , both prominent advocates for restrictions on transgender women competing in women’s sports.

The Missouri appearance therefore was unlikely to be viewed as an isolated fashion choice.

Message comes as Fever decision approaches

The timing also adds another angle to the story. Cunningham is heading into unrestricted free agency after playing the 2026 season on a one-year deal with Indiana, leaving her future with the Fever unresolved.

Her role with the team has grown beyond the box score, particularly through her physical style and willingness to defend teammates such as Caitlin Clark . That has also made her one of the more recognizable personalities on the roster.

Whether her public comments have any bearing on Indiana’s offseason decision remains uncertain. Supporters have praised Cunningham for speaking openly about her beliefs, while critics argue that her framing excludes transgender women and contributes to a deeply polarized debate.

Cunningham , however, has consistently presented her position as one centered on fairness and protection in women’s sports. Her latest appearance simply made clear that she still stands by the statement she's already made.

articles.standfirst: Clark is enjoying some downtime, but fans are already wondering what comes next for the Indiana Fever
articles.summary: Clark is enjoying some downtime, but fans are already wondering what comes next for the Indiana Fever
articles.body:
For the third time in her professional career, one of the league’s best players has failed to reach the playoffs. The Indiana Fever made the semifinals last year, but Caitlin Clark was unable to play after an injury kept her out for more than half the season.

For a player with Clark’s competitive mindset and desire to win, this early offseason is likely a difficult one . For now, she is doing what she enjoys most: slowing things down and taking a break at a time when the Fever may have more questions than answers.

A break to recharge, but plenty still needs to be decided

While the offseason gives Clark a chance to pause, recharge and come back stronger, there are still several unresolved moves around the Fever that could shape what comes next. A video of Clark enjoying some downtime has added to the speculation, with f ans wondering whether decisions have already been made that could change the dynamic between Clark, Sophie Cunningham and Lexie Hull.

Cunningham’s future is still uncertain after she signed a one-year deal with Indiana. There are also rumors surrounding a potential move for Hull, while Clark’s relationship with head coach Stephanie White does not appear to be improving despite the team’s efforts to suggest otherwise. The results have pointed in a different direction, especially with a roster that looked capable of winning with Clark back in the lineup.

Clark and Hull start the offseason together

The video showed Clark and Hull relaxed, spending time together as they began their break. Clark also returned to one of her favorite hobbies, joining Hull for a round of golf and showing that her swing is still on point.

But Cunningham’s absence from the trio immediately caught fans’ attention . She returned home to spend time with her family while also taking time for herself and waiting to decide what comes next. Last season, Cunningham made it clear that she was not happy about receiving only a one-year contract, meaning any new offer from Indiana could come with conditions from the star.

Meanwhile, Clark and Hull are starting the offseason together while they wait to see what moves come next. After the Fever failed to reach the semifinals this year, fans believe changes are needed , and Cunningham’s future is now one of the biggest questions surrounding the team.

articles.title: Early buyers of Caitlin Clark's Nike Caitlin 1s give them the thumbs up but have one small complaint
articles.standfirst: Caitlin Clark’s first Nike signature shoe is earning praise for comfort, traction and performance
articles.summary: Caitlin Clark’s first Nike signature shoe is earning praise for comfort, traction and performance
articles.body:
Caitlin Clark’s first Nike signature sneaker has made a strong opening statement, disappearing from Nike.com and several major retailers within roughly two hours of its October 1 U.S. launch.

The $140 Caitlin 1 arrived in Caitlin Blue and Warning Code colorways, and the rapid sellout gave Nike a welcome boost during a difficult stretch for the company. Nike is dealing with falling sales and its recent removal from the S&P 100, making a successful launch particularly encouraging.

The early reaction from customers suggests the excitement isn’t just due to Clark’s popularity. Nike’s review page shows the Caitlin 1 at 4.6 out of five stars, with shoppers highlighting comfort, cushioning, grip and support.

Reviewers have praised the shoe for feeling responsive during basketball while remaining comfortable enough for everyday wear.

The design is built around performance, too. Nike uses a lightweight Opticast upper, Cushlon foam and an Air Zoom Turbo unit, while Clark -specific touches include her No. 22, CC branding and messages celebrating her shooting range.

The combination of performance technology and Clark’s recognizable style appears to have helped the Caitlin 1 appeal to both basketball players and fans looking for an everyday sneaker.

Clark’s recent return to Iowa City added another layer to the launch. During ESPN’s College GameDay weekend, she celebrated her signature shoe with Hawkeye fans, while Nike hosted a temporary court and merchandise experience near campus.

The University of Iowa reported that fans lined up for hours to get the shoes, underscoring the level of interest surrounding Clark and her first signature release.

One small fit issue keeps coming up

There’s one criticism, however: the Caitlin 1 can feel snug. Some buyers say the shoe runs small, with the tighter fit particularly noticeable for people who have wider feet.

Others report that their usual size fits perfectly, so the issue doesn’t appear to affect everyone. Still, shoppers who are between sizes or prefer extra room may want to consider sizing up before purchasing.

That complaint hasn’t stopped the response from being strongly positive. Some early reviewers have singled out the court traction and stability, while others have focused on how comfortable the sneakers feel away from the hardwood.

One reviewer even described them as among the most comfortable basketball shoes they’d worn.

As for shoppers who missed the initial drop, another opportunity is coming. Nike lists the Hot Punch/Neo Pink “Midnight Fever” Caitlin 1 for an October 14 release.

With the first launch moving so quickly, buyers may want to have their size ready before the next colorway goes live.

The upcoming release also gives Nike another chance to build on the momentum created by the debut. Clark is expected to remain closely involved with promoting the line, with additional colorways planned for the months ahead.

If the positive reviews continue and sizing proves to be the only recurring complaint, the Caitlin 1 could have a strong foundation as Clark’s signature collection expands.
